features.name: #caller_location
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that captures the source location (file, line, column, procedure name) of the call site, returning a Source_Code_Location struct. Used as a default argument value to automatically fill location context at the point of invocation.
features.telemetry_use: Automatically inject call-site metadata into any procedure without manual logging — pass to allocators, loggers, assertion handlers to know exactly where allocations/errors occur. Zero-code instrumentation.
features.example: proc log_error(msg: string, loc := #caller_location) { fmt.println(msg, "at", loc.file_path, loc.line) }

features.name: #caller_expression
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that captures the textual source code expression of the argument at the call site (not its evaluated value). Returns a string.
features.telemetry_use: Record exactly what code the user wrote (e.g., "x + y") rather than its result; useful for assertion messages, metric labels, or debug output that preserves developer intent and makes traces human-readable.
features.example: assert :: proc(cond: bool, msg := #caller_expression(cond)) { if !cond { panic(msg) } }
features.source_ref: base:builtin (compiler intrinsic, not documented in runtime)

features.name: #procedure
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that expands to the name of the enclosing procedure as a string. Captured at the call site.
features.telemetry_use: Automatically tag log entries, assertions, and metrics with the function name; enables filtering/grouping telemetry by procedure without manual string literals.
features.example: when debug { fmt.println(#procedure, "called") }

features.name: #file
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that expands to the full file path of the current source file as a string.
features.telemetry_use: Tag observations with source file for cross-reference with version control or issue trackers; useful for pinpointing which module an event came from.
features.example: log_event("initialized in file: ", #file)

features.name: #line
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that expands to the line number of the current source location as an integer.
features.telemetry_use: Include line numbers in traces to correlate telemetry with exact source locations; combine with #file for precise issue reproduction.
features.example: trace(value, "at line ", #line)

features.name: #column
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that expands to the column number of the current source location as an integer.
features.telemetry_use: Fine-grained source pinpointing when multiple expressions exist on the same line; less common but useful for parsing-adjacent tools and detailed error reconstruction.
features.example: debug_location := Source_Code_Location{#file, #line, #column, #procedure}

features.name: Source_Code_Location
features.syntax: struct { file_path: string, line: i32, column: i32, procedure: string }
features.what_it_does: A struct that captures a precise source location: file path, line and column numbers, and the enclosing procedure name. Returned by #caller_location and used throughout the runtime for error context.
features.telemetry_use: Central data type for all telemetry snapshots that record 'where in code did this happen'. Fields can be serialized, indexed in time-series, or aggregated to heatmaps of high-activity code regions.
features.example: loc := Source_Code_Location{ file_path = "main.odin", line = 42, column = 5, procedure = "game_loop" }

features.name: type_info_of
features.what_it_does: Compile-time procedure that returns a pointer to the runtime Type_Info struct for a given type, including all metadata: size, alignment, field names/offsets (for structs), variant info (for unions), enum values, etc.
features.telemetry_use: Capture value metadata at runtime without manual reflection — iterate struct fields, print union tags, or serialize any value by walking its Type_Info. Enable generic value logging that works on any type.
features.example: info := type_info_of(MyStruct); for field_name in info.variant.(runtime.Type_Info_Struct).names { fmt.println(field_name) }

features.name: type_of
features.what_it_does: Compile-time procedure that returns the type of an expression (not its value). Used in compile-time type queries and assertions.
features.telemetry_use: Validate type assumptions at compile time to prevent runtime type mismatches in telemetry code; use in compile-time asserts to ensure logging procedures accept only expected types.
features.example: #assert(type_of(my_var) == i32)

features.name: typeid_of
features.what_it_does: Compile-time procedure that returns the typeid (unique identifier) for a type. Used to look up type information at runtime.
features.telemetry_use: Store compact type identifiers in telemetry records instead of full type names; use as a map key to aggregate values by type across sessions.
features.example: type_id := typeid_of(MyStruct); store_by_type[type_id] += value

features.name: size_of
features.what_it_does: Compile-time procedure that returns the size in bytes of a type.
features.telemetry_use: Auto-size telemetry buffers, calculate memory overhead of instrumentation, or validate struct field layouts before serializing telemetry data.
features.example: buffer := make([dynamic]u8, 0, size_of(Event))

features.name: align_of
features.what_it_does: Compile-time procedure that returns the alignment requirement in bytes of a type.
features.telemetry_use: Ensure telemetry records are packed/aligned for safe serialization to memory or disk; allocate aligned buffers for lock-free ring buffers used in high-frequency sampling.
features.example: assert(align_of(Event) <= CACHE_LINE_SIZE)

features.name: offset_of
features.syntax: offset_of(t.field) or offset_of(T, field) or offset_of(T, "field_name") -> uintptr
features.what_it_does: Compile-time procedure with overloads to get the byte offset of a struct field relative to struct start. Supports field name expressions, member references, or string names.
features.telemetry_use: Extract specific fields from packed telemetry structs without full deserialization; compute offsets for binary telemetry formats or memory-efficient samplers.
features.example: value_offset := offset_of(Event, "user_id"); user_id := cast(u64)raw_data[value_offset]

features.name: read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: Hardware instruction that reads the CPU cycle counter (rdtsc on x86, etc.). Returns raw cycle count, not wall-clock time. Extremely fast, nanosecond-resolution timing.
features.telemetry_use: Measure sub-microsecond latencies (e.g., frame time, per-draw-call cost, memory access patterns). Combine with read_cycle_counter_frequency to convert cycles to wall time. Ideal for frame-rate telemetry or lock-free performance profilers.
features.example: start := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter(); expensive_work(); elapsed_cycles := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter() - start

features.name: read_cycle_counter_frequency
features.what_it_does: Returns the CPU cycle frequency in Hz (e.g., 3.6 GHz = 3_600_000_000). Used to convert cycle counts to wall-clock time.
features.telemetry_use: Scale cycle measurements to nanoseconds or milliseconds for cross-platform telemetry aggregation. Called once at startup; remains constant for the run.
features.example: frequency := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter_frequency(); ns_elapsed := (cycles * 1_000_000_000) / frequency

features.name: #load_directory
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that reads all files from a directory and embeds them as an array of Load_Directory_File structs (each with name: string, data: []byte). Evaluated at compile time.
features.telemetry_use: Embed telemetry schemas, format strings, or metadata tables (enums, field names, type mappings) into the binary at compile time; use in codegen for strongly-typed telemetry serializers or decoders.
features.example: embedded_files := #load_directory("telemetry_schemas/"); for file in embedded_files { process_schema(file.name, file.data) }

features.name: Logger_Proc
features.syntax: #type proc(data: rawptr, level: Logger_Level, text: string, options: Logger_Options, location := #caller_location)
features.what_it_does: A callback function type (procedure pointer) used by context.logger. Invoked whenever log() is called. Receives log level, text, options (what to include: date, time, file, line, procedure, color, thread id), and automatic caller location.
features.telemetry_use: Implement custom telemetry backends (disk, network, memory ring buffer) by defining a Logger_Proc and setting context.logger. Caller location is passed automatically; proc can filter/buffer by level or tag events by source.
features.example: my_logger :: proc(data: rawptr, level: Logger_Level, text: string, options: Logger_Options, location := #caller_location) { custom_sink[level] << location.procedure << text }

features.name: Logger_Level
features.syntax: enum uint { Debug=0, Info=10, Warning=20, Error=30, Fatal=40 }
features.what_it_does: Enum of log severity levels. Used to filter/route log messages in Logger_Proc callbacks.
features.telemetry_use: Categorize telemetry events by severity; enable/disable collection per level at runtime via context.logger.lowest_level. Enables cost-free high-volume debug logs that are compiled away in prod.
features.example: if context.logger.lowest_level <= .Debug { log_details() }

features.name: Logger_Option
features.syntax: enum { Level, Date, Time, Short_File_Path, Long_File_Path, Line, Procedure, Terminal_Color, Thread_Id }
features.what_it_does: Bit flags that control what metadata is included in log output (passed to Logger_Proc).
features.telemetry_use: Selectively include/exclude metadata in telemetry streams — e.g., enable Thread_Id only in multi-threaded builds, or disable Terminal_Color for binary formats. Configurable per logger instance.
features.example: context.logger.options = {.Procedure, .Line, .Thread_Id}

features.name: Allocator_Proc
features.syntax: #type proc(allocator_data: rawptr, mode: Allocator_Mode, size, alignment: int, old_memory: rawptr, old_size: int, location: Source_Code_Location = #caller_location) -> ([]byte, Allocator_Error)
features.what_it_does: A callback function type for custom memory allocators. Receives allocation request (mode, size, alignment), old pointer/size (for resizes), and automatic caller location.
features.telemetry_use: Instrument memory allocation with telemetry — log all allocations with call site, track high-allocation hot spots, detect fragmentation. Caller location enables per-source memory budgeting.
features.example: custom_alloc :: proc(data: rawptr, mode: Allocator_Mode, size, alignment: int, old_mem: rawptr, old_size: int, location := #caller_location) -> ([]byte, Allocator_Error) { log_alloc(location, size); return default_allocator_proc(...) }

features.name: Context
features.syntax: struct { allocator: Allocator, temp_allocator: Allocator, assertion_failure_proc: Assertion_Failure_Proc, logger: Logger, random_generator: Random_Generator, user_ptr: rawptr, user_index: int }
features.what_it_does: Runtime context struct. Holds callbacks for memory allocation, logging, assertions, and RNG. Passed implicitly to all Odin procedures; can be set per-thread.
features.telemetry_use: Swap in a custom logger, allocator, or assertion handler to instrument a whole program in one place. user_ptr/user_index fields can store telemetry state (e.g., frame number, trace buffer ptr). Thread-local context enables per-thread telemetry.
features.example: context.logger = make_my_telemetry_logger(); context.user_index = current_frame

features.name: Type_Info
features.syntax: struct { size: int, align: int, flags: Type_Info_Flags, id: typeid, variant: union {...} }
features.what_it_does: Runtime type metadata struct. Contains size/alignment and a tagged union with type-specific info: Named, Integer, Pointer, Struct, Union, Enum, Array, Map, etc. Each variant holds field names, offsets, enum values, etc.
features.telemetry_use: Walk any value's structure at runtime — serialize arbitrary structs to JSON/protobuf, build generic value pretty-printers, or auto-generate telemetry codecs for all types in a program.
features.example: info := type_info_of(MyEvent); if s, ok := info.variant.(runtime.Type_Info_Struct); ok { for name in s.names { field_val := read_at(event_ptr, s.offsets[idx]) } }

features.name: Type_Info_Struct
features.syntax: struct { types: [^]^Type_Info, names: [^]string, offsets: [^]uintptr, usings: [^]bool, tags: [^]string, field_count: i32, flags: Type_Info_Struct_Flags, soa_kind, soa_len, soa_base_type }
features.what_it_does: Variant of Type_Info for struct types. Parallel arrays: field types, names, byte offsets, using flags, and struct tags. Enables field-by-field reflection.
features.telemetry_use: Serialize telemetry event structs to compact binary or text by iterating fields; use offsets to extract values from raw memory; use tags to mark sensitive or sampled fields.
features.example: s := info.variant.(runtime.Type_Info_Struct); for i in 0..<s.field_count { offset := s.offsets[i]; name := s.names[i]; value := mem.ptr_offset(event_ptr, int(offset)) }

features.name: #assert
features.what_it_does: Compile-time assertion. Evaluated at compile time; if false, compilation fails with an error message.
features.telemetry_use: Validate telemetry invariants at compile time (e.g., telemetry event size, type compatibility, field ordering). Fail early in the build if instrumentation setup is incorrect.
features.example: #assert(size_of(Event) <= MAX_EVENT_SIZE, "Event too large for ring buffer")

features.name: #sparse
features.what_it_does: Compile-time type directive that creates a sparse array indexed by enum values. Only stores entries for explicitly-set enum keys; saves memory vs. full dense array.
features.telemetry_use: Accumulate per-event-type metrics, per-thread counters, or per-state timings using a sparse map-like structure that's type-safe and zero-copy at init.
features.example: event_counts := #sparse[Event_Type]i64 { .Frame_Start = 0, .Frame_End = 0 }; event_counts[evt_type] += 1

features.name: type_info_of
features.what_it_does: Retrieves the runtime Type_Info descriptor for a given typeid, enabling generic introspection of types at runtime. Core foundation for all runtime reflection.
features.telemetry_use: Lookup type metadata for any value: retrieve field names/offsets/types, variant info for unions, enum value mappings. Essential for logging any value generically.
features.example: ti := type_info_of(typeid_of(x)); fmt.println(ti.size, ti.align)

features.name: typeid_of
features.what_it_does: Compiler builtin that returns the typeid of a given type or value, representing its unique type identifier at runtime.
features.telemetry_use: Capture runtime type identity for tagging logged values with their exact type. Required to feed into type_info_of.
features.example: id := typeid_of(42); // id now represents the type of the literal

features.name: type_kind
features.what_it_does: Returns an enum Type_Kind (Integer, Float, Struct, Enum, Union, etc.) classifying what kind of type a typeid represents, stripping none of the named/distinct layers.
features.telemetry_use: Branch on type category to decide how to capture/serialize a value (e.g., different path for structs vs enums vs primitives).
features.example: match type_kind(MyType) { case .Struct: ..., case .Enum: ... }

features.name: type_info_base
features.what_it_does: Strips one level of `distinct` wrapping from a Type_Info, returning the underlying type. Named types (distinct) point to a base type via a Type_Info_Named variant.
features.telemetry_use: Canonicalize types before inspecting fields/variants—necessary because distinct types wrap the actual struct/union/enum info.
features.example: base := type_info_base(type_info_of(MyDistinctType)); // unwrap distinct layer

features.name: type_info_core
features.what_it_does: Strips all layers of `distinct` AND unwraps enums/bit_sets to their backing integer type. Reaches the true base representation.
features.telemetry_use: Normalize types to their semantic core for comparative logging or canonical serialization across distinct aliases.
features.example: core := type_info_core(ti); // unwrap distinct + enum backing

features.name: struct_field_at
features.what_it_does: Returns a Struct_Field containing name, type, tag, byte offset, and is_using flag for field index i of struct type T.
features.telemetry_use: Enumerate struct fields by index to capture all field names and offsets for walk-the-struct introspection; extract struct tags for telemetry hints.
features.example: f := struct_field_at(MyStruct, 0); fmt.println(f.name, f.offset, f.type)

features.name: struct_field_by_name
features.what_it_does: Returns Struct_Field for a named field of struct type T, or a zero-initialized field if not found.
features.telemetry_use: Look up a specific field by name to log its value and metadata without iterating all fields.
features.example: f := struct_field_by_name(MyStruct, "position"); value := reflect.struct_field_value_by_name(obj, "position")

features.name: struct_field_value_by_name
features.syntax: struct_field_value_by_name(a: any, field: string, allow_using := false) -> any
features.what_it_does: Extracts the value of a named field from a struct-like `any`, returning an `any` pointing to that field's data and typeid. Optionally recurses into `using` fields.
features.telemetry_use: Retrieve arbitrary struct field values at runtime for capturing in telemetry records. Core operation for generic struct inspection.
features.example: pos := struct_field_value_by_name(entity, "position"); x, _ := as_f32(reflect.index(pos, 0))

features.name: struct_field_value
features.what_it_does: Extracts the value of a field from a struct-like `any` using a Struct_Field descriptor, returning an `any` of the field's data.
features.telemetry_use: Retrieve field value given a pre-looked-up Struct_Field (e.g., from struct_field_at in a loop).
features.example: field := struct_field_at(MyStruct, i); val := struct_field_value(obj, field)

features.name: struct_field_names
features.what_it_does: Returns a slice of all field names for a struct type T.
features.telemetry_use: Get all field names to iterate and log struct contents by name.
features.example: names := struct_field_names(MyStruct); for n in names { fmt.println(n) }

features.name: struct_field_types
features.what_it_does: Returns a slice of ^Type_Info for all fields of struct type T.
features.telemetry_use: Retrieve type metadata for all struct fields to determine serialization strategy per field.
features.example: types := struct_field_types(MyStruct); for t in types { fmt.println(t.size) }

features.name: struct_field_tags
features.what_it_does: Returns a slice of Struct_Tag for all fields of struct type T, allowing inspection of struct tags.
features.telemetry_use: Extract telemetry hints from struct field tags (e.g., `telemetry:"skip"`, `telemetry:"name=custom_name"`) to configure per-field logging behavior.
features.example: tags := struct_field_tags(MyStruct); for t, i in tags { if v, ok := struct_tag_lookup(t, "telemetry"); ok { ... } }

features.name: struct_field_offsets
features.what_it_does: Returns a slice of byte offsets (relative to struct base) for all fields of struct type T.
features.telemetry_use: Manually compute field pointers when walking struct memory, e.g., to capture field-level snapshots over time.
features.example: offsets := struct_field_offsets(MyStruct); field_ptr := rawptr(uintptr(obj_ptr) + offsets[i])

features.name: struct_field_count
features.what_it_does: Counts fields in a struct type T using one of three methods: .Top_Level (direct fields only), .Using (include using-embedded struct field counts), .Recursive (count all nested fields transitively).
features.telemetry_use: Determine loop bounds or allocation size when capturing all struct fields generically.
features.example: count := struct_field_count(MyStruct, .Recursive); // allocate capture buffer for all nested fields

features.name: struct_fields_zipped
features.what_it_does: Returns a #soa (struct-of-arrays) slice of Struct_Field for all fields of type T, convenient for parallel iteration over names, types, tags, offsets, and is_using flags.
features.telemetry_use: Iterate all struct fields with their metadata in parallel (one for-in loop) for efficient batch capture.
features.example: for field, i in struct_fields_zipped(MyStruct) { fmt.println(field.name, field.offset, field.tag) }

features.name: struct_tag_lookup
features.syntax: struct_tag_lookup(tag: Struct_Tag, key: string) -> (value: string, ok: bool)
features.what_it_does: Parses a struct tag (key:"value" space-separated format) and returns the value for a given key, or (empty, false) if not found.
features.telemetry_use: Extract telemetry directives from struct field tags (e.g., `trace:"per_frame"`, `group:"audio_subsystem"`) to configure capturing behavior.
features.example: if v, ok := struct_tag_lookup(tag, "trace"); ok { log_per_frame = (v == "per_frame") }

features.name: enum_string
features.what_it_does: Returns the name string of an enum value carried in `any`. Panics if not an enum.
features.telemetry_use: Convert enum values to human-readable names for logging without manual mapping.
features.example: fmt.println("State:", reflect.enum_string(state_value))

features.name: enum_from_name
features.syntax: enum_from_name(Enum_Type: typeid, name: string) -> (value: Enum_Type, ok: bool)
features.what_it_does: Looks up an enum value by name and returns it (or 0, false if not found). Parametrically polymorphic.
features.telemetry_use: Parse enum names from config or external input to set telemetry filters/flags at runtime.
features.example: state, ok := reflect.enum_from_name(State, "Running")

features.name: enum_from_name_any
features.syntax: enum_from_name_any(Enum_Type: typeid, name: string) -> (value: Type_Info_Enum_Value, ok: bool)
features.what_it_does: Looks up an enum value by name at runtime (without compile-time type information), returning a generic enum value.
features.telemetry_use: Resolve enum names generically when type information is only available via reflection.
features.example: val, ok := reflect.enum_from_name_any(enum_type_id, "SomeValue")

features.name: enum_name_from_value
features.what_it_does: Returns the name of an enum value (typed). Parametrically polymorphic.
features.telemetry_use: Convert a typed enum value to its name string for telemetry output.
features.example: name, ok := reflect.enum_name_from_value(State.Running); fmt.println(name)

features.name: enum_name_from_value_any
features.what_it_does: Returns the name of an enum value carried in `any`. Reflection-based version.
features.telemetry_use: Convert an `any` enum to its name when type is known only at runtime.
features.example: name, ok := reflect.enum_name_from_value_any(enum_any); fmt.println(name)

features.name: enum_field_names
features.what_it_does: Returns a slice of all enum value names for a given enum type.
features.telemetry_use: Enumerate all possible enum values to generate telemetry schemas or validate parsed enum input.
features.example: names := reflect.enum_field_names(State); // ["Idle", "Running", "Paused"]

features.name: enum_field_values
features.what_it_does: Returns a slice of all enum values (as i64 or u64) for a given enum type.
features.telemetry_use: Get raw numeric enum values paired with names for bidirectional name↔value mapping in telemetry.
features.example: vals := reflect.enum_field_values(State); // parallel with enum_field_names(State)

features.name: enum_fields_zipped
features.what_it_does: Returns a #soa slice pairing all enum names and values for parallel iteration.
features.telemetry_use: Iterate name-value pairs in one loop for efficient enum schema generation or validation.
features.example: for field, i in reflect.enum_fields_zipped(State) { fmt.println(field.name, field.value) }

features.name: union_variant_typeid
features.what_it_does: Returns the typeid of the currently active variant in a union `any`. UNSAFE: reads and interprets the union tag.
features.telemetry_use: Identify which variant is active in a union to decide how to capture/serialize it.
features.example: active_id := reflect.union_variant_typeid(my_union); fmt.println(reflect.write_typeid({}, active_id))

features.name: get_union_variant
features.what_it_does: Returns an `any` of the currently active variant's data and typeid in a union `any`.
features.telemetry_use: Extract the active variant as an `any` for further introspection or logging.
features.example: variant := reflect.get_union_variant(my_union); fmt.println(variant)

features.name: get_union_variant_raw_tag
features.what_it_does: Returns the raw tag value (integer) of the currently active variant in a union `any`. UNSAFE.
features.telemetry_use: Capture the union tag as metadata (for diff-based or sparse logging of union changes).
features.example: tag := reflect.get_union_variant_raw_tag(my_union); fmt.println("tag:", tag)

features.name: as_bytes
features.what_it_does: Reinterprets the data of an `any` as a byte slice covering the entire type size.
features.telemetry_use: Capture raw binary representation of a value for serialization or binary hashing.
features.example: bytes := reflect.as_bytes(my_value); for b in bytes { fmt.print_byte(b) }

features.name: as_i64
features.what_it_does: Attempts to convert an `any` integer/float/boolean/complex/quaternion to i64. Returns (value, false) if conversion not possible.
features.telemetry_use: Normalize integer-like values to a common i64 representation for logging without type dispatch.
features.example: i, ok := reflect.as_i64(some_int); if ok { fmt.println(i) }

features.name: as_u64
features.what_it_does: Attempts to convert an `any` integer/float/boolean/complex/quaternion to u64. Returns (value, false) if not possible.
features.telemetry_use: Normalize unsigned integer-like values to u64 for unified logging.
features.example: u, ok := reflect.as_u64(some_uint); if ok { fmt.println(u) }

features.name: as_f64
features.what_it_does: Attempts to convert an `any` integer/float/boolean/complex/quaternion to f64. Returns (value, false) if not possible.
features.telemetry_use: Normalize numeric values to f64 for floating-point telemetry (e.g., performance metrics, deltas).
features.example: f, ok := reflect.as_f64(some_number); if ok { fmt.println(f) }

features.name: as_bool
features.what_it_does: Attempts to convert an `any` boolean to bool. Returns (value, false) if not a boolean type.
features.telemetry_use: Extract boolean flags from telemetry control structs.
features.example: enabled, ok := reflect.as_bool(flag_value); if ok && enabled { ... }

features.name: as_string
features.what_it_does: Attempts to convert an `any` string or cstring to string. Returns ("", false) if not a string type.
features.telemetry_use: Extract string labels/names from reflected values for telemetry context.
features.example: s, ok := reflect.as_string(name_value); if ok { fmt.println(s) }

features.name: as_pointer
features.what_it_does: Attempts to extract a raw pointer from pointer types (^T, [^]T, cstring, cstring16). Returns (nil, false) if not a pointer-like type.
features.telemetry_use: Capture pointer addresses for tracking allocations, lifetimes, or dereferencing in telemetry.
features.example: ptr, ok := reflect.as_pointer(ptr_value); if ok { fmt.println_uint(uintptr(ptr)) }

features.name: as_raw_data
features.what_it_does: Attempts to extract raw data pointers from container types (string, array, slice, dynamic array). Returns (nil, false) if not a container.
features.telemetry_use: Access underlying buffer pointers for capturing collection contents or metadata (length, capacity) in telemetry records.
features.example: data, ok := reflect.as_raw_data(array_value); if ok { len := reflect.length(array_value) }

features.name: length
features.what_it_does: Returns the length of array-like types (^T, [N]T, []T, [dynamic]T, map, string/cstring, string16/cstring16, #simd). Returns 0 if not applicable.
features.telemetry_use: Determine collection size for iterating and capturing all elements, or for size-based telemetry (e.g., "list had 50 items").
features.example: n := reflect.length(my_array); for i in 0..<n { elem := reflect.index(my_array, i) }

features.name: capacity
features.what_it_does: Returns the capacity of dynamic types (^T, [N]T, [dynamic]T, [dynamic; N]T, map, #simd). Returns 0 if not applicable.
features.telemetry_use: Capture allocation efficiency (length vs capacity ratio) for memory/performance telemetry.
features.example: cap := reflect.capacity(dyn_array); util := f64(reflect.length(dyn_array)) / f64(cap)

features.name: index
features.syntax: index(val: any, i: int, loc := #caller_location) -> any
features.what_it_does: Dynamically indexes into an array-like `any`, returning an `any` of the i-th element. Bounds-checks and returns nil on failure.
features.telemetry_use: Iterate collection elements generically when walking arrays/slices/dynamic arrays at runtime.

features.name: reflect.struct_field_value
features.what_it_does: Returns an `any` holding the value of a struct field given a Struct_Field descriptor
features.telemetry_use: Convert Struct_Field + parent value to field any, generic field capture pipeline, zero-copy field extraction
features.example: field := reflect.struct_field_at(T, 0); field_any := reflect.struct_field_value(my_struct_any, field)

features.name: reflect.struct_field_count
features.what_it_does: Returns the field count of struct T by method (.Top_Level, .Using, or .Recursive)
features.telemetry_use: Validation of struct schema, pre-allocate capture buffers, versioning checks (expect N fields)
features.example: count := reflect.struct_field_count(MyStruct); assert(count == 3)

features.name: reflect.struct_fields_zipped
features.what_it_does: Returns all struct fields as an #soa slice (struct-of-arrays) for efficient iteration
features.telemetry_use: High-performance struct field enumeration, cache-friendly iteration, build field descriptor tables
features.example: for field, i in reflect.struct_fields_zipped(MyStruct) { fmt.println(field.name, field.offset) }

features.name: reflect.struct_field_names
features.what_it_does: Returns slice of all field names for struct T
features.telemetry_use: Generate telemetry column headers, build field name lists for config/filtering, human-readable schema
features.example: names := reflect.struct_field_names(MyStruct); for name in names { /* emit column */ }

features.name: reflect.struct_field_types
features.what_it_does: Returns slice of all field Type_Infos for struct T
features.telemetry_use: Type routing per field, build type-specific capture templates, schema inference
features.example: types := reflect.struct_field_types(MyStruct); for ti, i in types { /* dispatch by type */ }

features.name: reflect.struct_field_offsets
features.what_it_does: Returns slice of all field offsets (in bytes) for struct T
features.telemetry_use: Build offset lookup tables, pointer arithmetic for field extraction, memory layout analysis
features.example: offsets := reflect.struct_field_offsets(MyStruct); ptr := rawptr(uintptr(base) + offsets[0])

features.name: reflect.length
features.what_it_does: Returns the length of indexable/sized any value (arrays, slices, dynamic arrays, maps, strings, SIMD vectors)
features.telemetry_use: Capture collection sizes, enable length-based filtering/sampling, detect collection size anomalies
features.example: len := reflect.length(my_array_any); for i in 0..<len { ... }

features.name: reflect.capacity
features.what_it_does: Returns the capacity of dynamic arrays, maps, and SIMD vectors
features.telemetry_use: Measure collection overhead (cap vs len), detect allocator fragmentation, memory efficiency metrics
features.example: cap := reflect.capacity(my_dyn_array_any); overhead := cap - reflect.length(my_dyn_array_any)

features.name: reflect.index
features.syntax: index(val: any, i: int, loc: Source_Code_Location = #caller_location) -> any
features.what_it_does: Dynamically indexes any indexable value and returns the element as any
features.telemetry_use: Generic indexed value capture, element-by-element array instrumentation, bounds-checked telemetry access
features.example: elem_any := reflect.index(my_array_any, 5); fmt.println(elem_any)

features.name: reflect.enum_string
features.what_it_does: Returns the symbolic name of an enum value
features.telemetry_use: Emit human-readable enum names in telemetry, reverse-map enum values to identifiers, state string representation
features.example: name := reflect.enum_string(my_enum_any); fmt.println(name)

features.name: reflect.as_bytes
features.what_it_does: Reinterprets the any value as a byte slice
features.telemetry_use: Serialize any value to bytes for transport, binary telemetry encoding, zero-copy raw data capture
features.example: bytes := reflect.as_bytes(my_struct_any); send_to_telemetry_backend(bytes)

features.name: reflect.size_of_typeid
features.what_it_does: Returns the size of a type given its typeid (via Type_Info)
features.telemetry_use: Runtime size queries, allocate typed buffers, validate type assumptions
features.example: sz := reflect.size_of_typeid(MyStruct); buf := make([dynamic]u8, sz)

features.name: reflect.align_of_typeid
features.what_it_does: Returns the alignment of a type given its typeid
features.telemetry_use: Respect type alignment for serialization, allocate aligned buffers, zero-copy capture
features.example: align := reflect.align_of_typeid(MyStruct)

features.name: reflect.type_kind
features.what_it_does: Returns a Type_Kind enum classifying a typeid (Named, Integer, Struct, Array, Union, etc.)
features.telemetry_use: Single switch on type classification, dispatch to specialized capture logic by kind
features.example: switch reflect.type_kind(T) { case .Struct: /* struct capture */ case .Array: /* array capture */ ... }

features.name: Context
features.syntax: Context :: struct { allocator: Allocator, temp_allocator: Allocator, assertion_failure_proc: Assertion_Failure_Proc, logger: Logger, random_generator: Random_Generator, user_ptr: rawptr, user_index: int, _internal: rawptr }
features.what_it_does: Core thread-local runtime context holding allocators, logger, random generator, and two custom user fields (user_ptr + user_index) for stashing per-thread telemetry state. All procedures implicitly receive this and can access/mutate it. The _internal field is compiler-reserved.
features.telemetry_use: Stash custom telemetry collectors/buffers in user_ptr (cast to your telemetry struct) and use user_index as a frame counter or thread ID. Avoids globals by storing per-thread state in the implicit context.
features.example: custom_telemetry := cast(^Telemetry_State)context.user_ptr; custom_telemetry.frame_count += 1

features.name: Source_Code_Location
features.syntax: Source_Code_Location :: struct { file_path: string, line, column: i32, procedure: string }
features.what_it_does: Captures call site metadata: file, line, column, and enclosing procedure name. Automatically populated by #caller_location directive at compile time; not a runtime feature.
features.telemetry_use: Attach source location to every telemetry event to identify which code path generated the observation. Enables pinpoint debugging and call-graph reconstruction.
features.example: log_value :: proc(name: string, val: int, loc := #caller_location) { telem.events = append(telem.events, {location=loc, name, value=val}) }

features.name: #caller_location
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that injects the Source_Code_Location of the caller into a procedure's default parameter. When a caller invokes proc(x, y), the #caller_location parameter is automatically filled with that caller's loc.
features.telemetry_use: Automatically instrument all call sites with source location without manual annotation. Enables zero-overhead-when-disabled pattern: if you compile without telemetry callbacks, the location injection vanishes.
features.example: Logger_Proc :: #type proc(data: rawptr, level: Logger_Level, text: string, options: Logger_Options, location := #caller_location)

features.name: Allocator
features.syntax: Allocator :: struct { procedure: Allocator_Proc, data: rawptr } where Allocator_Proc :: #type proc(allocator_data: rawptr, mode: Allocator_Mode, size, alignment: int, old_memory: rawptr, old_size: int, location: Source_Code_Location = #caller_location) -> ([]byte, Allocator_Error)
features.what_it_does: Custom memory allocator with pluggable procedure. Receives Allocator_Mode (Alloc, Free, Free_All, Resize, Query_Features, Query_Info, Alloc_Non_Zeroed, Resize_Non_Zeroed) and caller location. Can be swapped per-context.
features.telemetry_use: Replace context.allocator with a telemetry-aware allocator that logs all allocs/frees with sizes and caller locations. Enables memory profiling and leak detection. Query_Info mode allows querying allocation metadata.
features.example: my_allocator_proc :: proc(allocator_data: rawptr, mode: runtime.Allocator_Mode, size, alignment: int, old_memory: rawptr, old_size: int, location := #caller_location) -> ([]byte, runtime.Allocator_Error) { if mode == .Alloc { telem.record_alloc(size, location) } ... }

features.name: Allocator_Mode
features.syntax: Allocator_Mode :: enum byte { Alloc, Free, Free_All, Resize, Query_Features, Query_Info, Alloc_Non_Zeroed, Resize_Non_Zeroed }
features.what_it_does: Enum dispatching different allocator operations. Query_Features and Query_Info allow the allocator to report capabilities and query metadata about prior allocations.
features.telemetry_use: Discriminate on mode in a custom allocator to selectively capture alloc/free events. Query_Info enables post-hoc allocation tracking without re-intercepting old pointers.
features.example: switch mode { case .Alloc: /* record */ case .Query_Info: /* populate Allocator_Query_Info */ ... }

features.name: Logger
features.syntax: Logger :: struct { procedure: Logger_Proc, data: rawptr, lowest_level: Logger_Level, options: Logger_Options } where Logger_Proc :: #type proc(data: rawptr, level: Logger_Level, text: string, options: Logger_Options, location := #caller_location)
features.what_it_does: Pluggable structured logging framework. Receives log level, text, options (bit set controlling what metadata to include: Level, Date, Time, File, Line, Procedure, Terminal_Color, Thread_Id), and caller location.
features.telemetry_use: Replace context.logger with a custom logger that emits telemetry events (structured, timestamped, with file/line/procedure). Logger_Option bits let you select which metadata to capture at runtime.
features.example: my_logger_proc :: proc(data: rawptr, level: runtime.Logger_Level, text: string, options: runtime.Logger_Options, location := #caller_location) { telem.record_log(level, text, location, options) }

features.name: Logger_Level
features.syntax: Logger_Level :: enum uint { Debug=0, Info=10, Warning=20, Error=30, Fatal=40 }
features.what_it_does: Log severity level. Numeric values (0,10,20...) allow easy filtering by threshold.
features.telemetry_use: Record event severity in telemetry stream. Enable/disable capture based on level (e.g., only capture Error+ in production).
features.example: context.logger.lowest_level = .Info  // only log Info and above

features.name: Assertion_Failure_Proc
features.syntax: Assertion_Failure_Proc :: #type proc(prefix, message: string, loc: Source_Code_Location) -> !
features.what_it_does: Pluggable assertion handler. Called when an assertion fails; must not return (note the ! return type indicating noreturn). Receives assertion prefix/message and precise source location.
features.telemetry_use: Intercept all assertion failures with telemetry: log the failure, capture stack, report to telemetry backend before crashing. Provides crash/error event with exact assertion location.
features.example: my_assertion_handler :: proc(prefix, message: string, loc: Source_Code_Location) -> ! { telem.record_assertion_failure(message, loc); panic(message) }

features.name: Random_Generator
features.syntax: Random_Generator :: struct { procedure: Random_Generator_Proc, data: rawptr } where Random_Generator_Proc :: #type proc(data: rawptr, mode: Random_Generator_Mode, p: []byte)
features.what_it_does: Pluggable PRNG. Modes: Read (fill buffer with random bytes), Reset (reseed), Query_Info (report capabilities like Cryptographic, Uniform, External_Entropy, Resettable).
features.telemetry_use: Deterministic seeding for reproducible telemetry traces. Store seed in telemetry header so replays get same random values. Query_Info can report if PRNG is seeded.
features.example: seed_prng_from_telemetry :: proc() { context.random_generator.procedure(context.random_generator.data, .Reset, telemetry_seed[:]) }

features.name: default_context
features.what_it_does: Allocates and initializes a default Context struct with no-op allocators, default logger, and default assertion handler. Contextless calling convention (no implicit context dependency).
features.telemetry_use: Create a fresh telemetry-enabled context snapshot for spawning worker threads or isolated scopes. Store as baseline to detect context mutations.
features.example: ctx := runtime.default_context(); ctx.user_ptr = my_telemetry_state; context = ctx

features.name: Tick
features.what_it_does: Opaque monotonic time snapshot (nanosecond precision, not wall-clock). Used for measuring elapsed duration between two points.
features.telemetry_use: Timestamp telemetry events with high-resolution monotonic time. Immune to clock adjustments; safe for measuring deltas.
features.example: start := time.tick_now(); do_work(); elapsed := time.tick_since(start)

features.name: tick_now
features.what_it_does: Capture current monotonic time as a Tick. Contextless, zero-overhead, typically a single CPU instruction (read_cycle_counter or similar).
features.telemetry_use: Obtain high-resolution event timestamps for all telemetry samples. Call at observation points to log when a value was recorded.
features.example: event := Telemetry_Event{timestamp=time.tick_now(), value=42, name="frame_time"}

features.name: tick_since
features.what_it_does: Calculate Duration (i64 nanoseconds) from a prior Tick to now. Handles wraparound on platforms with 32-bit counters.
features.telemetry_use: Measure elapsed time for scoped operations: frame time, task latency, etc. Record duration deltas as telemetry values.
features.example: frame_start := time.tick_now(); render(); frame_dur := time.tick_since(frame_start); telem.record("frame_ms", f64(frame_dur) / 1_000_000)

features.name: SCOPED_TICK_DURATION
features.what_it_does: Deferred scope annotation macro. On entry captures Tick; on exit (via _tick_duration_end callback) stores elapsed Duration into *d. Syntactic sugar for measuring a block.
features.telemetry_use: Inline scope-duration measurement without manual tick bookkeeping. Pairs with deferred to auto-record on exit.
features.example: { SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&my_dur); do_work() }  // my_dur now holds elapsed time

features.name: read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: Read CPU's timestamp counter (TSC on x86, cycle counter on ARM). Raw, unscaled cycle count. Contextless; typically 1-2 cycles.
features.telemetry_use: Lowest-overhead event timestamp (even cheaper than tick_now for sub-microsecond granularity). Requires dividing by tsc_frequency to convert to nanoseconds.
features.example: cycle := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter(); /* later */ cycles_per_ns := tsc_freq / 1_000_000_000; elapsed_ns := (intrinsics.read_cycle_counter() - cycle) / cycles_per_ns

features.name: read_cycle_counter_frequency
features.what_it_does: Query the CPU's TSC or cycle counter frequency in Hz. Platform-dependent; may fail on older CPUs or VMs.
features.telemetry_use: Calibrate raw cycle counts to nanoseconds or wall-clock time. Store in telemetry header for offline trace analysis.
features.example: hz := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter_frequency(); ns_per_cycle := 1_000_000_000 / hz

features.name: has_invariant_tsc
features.what_it_does: Check if CPU has invariant TSC (constant frequency TSC independent of P-states). Modern x86-64 and ARM64 return true.
features.telemetry_use: Validate TSC-based timing is reliable before using raw cycle counts. If false, fall back to tick_now() which uses OS time.
features.example: if time.has_invariant_tsc() { use_tsc_timestamps() } else { use_os_timestamps() }

features.name: tsc_frequency
features.what_it_does: Obtain CPU TSC frequency in Hz. Tries OS query first; falls back to sleep-calibration if needed. Returns (freq_hz, ok). Fallback sleep duration is tunable.
features.telemetry_use: On startup, measure and cache tsc_frequency to calibrate raw cycle counts. Store in telemetry metadata for replay scripts.
features.example: hz, ok := time.tsc_frequency(time.Second); if ok { telemetry_header.tsc_hz = hz }

features.name: type_info_of (runtime package)
features.what_it_does: Look up Type_Info struct from a typeid. Contains all metadata: size, alignment, flags, and a discriminated union of type-specific info (struct fields, enum values, etc.). Contextless.
features.telemetry_use: Inspect types at runtime to serialize arbitrary values: walk struct fields, array elements, map kv pairs. Enables generic telemetry value capture and export.
features.example: ti := runtime.type_info_of(typeid_of(my_struct)); if info, ok := ti.variant.(runtime.Type_Info_Struct); ok { for field_name in info.names { ... } }

features.name: Type_Info
features.syntax: Type_Info :: struct { size: int, align: int, flags: Type_Info_Flags, id: typeid, variant: union { Type_Info_Named, Type_Info_Integer, ... Type_Info_Struct, ... } }
features.what_it_does: Runtime reflection metadata for any type. Size/align/flags are universal; variant is a discriminated union for type-specific data (struct fields, enum values, procedure signatures, etc.).
features.telemetry_use: Walk struct fields to serialize complex values into telemetry format. Inspect union variants to log discriminated types. Match on Type_Info_Struct to enumerate fields by name.
features.example: ti := runtime.type_info_of(typeid_of(Point)); struct_info := ti.variant.(runtime.Type_Info_Struct); for i in 0 ..< struct_info.field_count { field_name := struct_info.names[i]; field_type := struct_info.types[i] }

features.name: Type_Info_Struct
features.syntax: Type_Info_Struct :: struct { backing_type: ^Type_Info, names: [^]string, types: [^]^Type_Info, bit_sizes: [^]uintptr, bit_offsets: [^]uintptr, tags: [^]string, field_count: int }
features.what_it_does: Metadata for struct types. Lists field names, types, and offsets (both bit and byte). Enables field-by-field reflection.
features.telemetry_use: Enumerate and serialize all fields of a struct value: for each field, get name+type, compute pointer via bit_offset, read value, emit telemetry.
features.example: for i in 0 ..< struct_info.field_count { name := struct_info.names[i]; field_ptr := uintptr(my_ptr) + struct_info.bit_offsets[i]/8; field_val := cast(i32)field_ptr^  // example for i32 field }

features.name: type_kind
features.syntax: type_kind :: proc(T: typeid) -> Type_Kind where Type_Kind :: enum { Invalid, Named, Integer, Rune, Float, ..., Struct, Union, ... }
features.what_it_does: Map a typeid to a high-level kind enum (Struct, Integer, Slice, etc.). Used to branch on how to inspect or serialize a type.
features.telemetry_use: Dispatch serialization logic by type kind: structs walk fields, slices iterate elements, integers format as decimal, etc.
features.example: kind := reflect.type_kind(typeid_of(my_val)); if kind == .Struct { /* walk fields */ } else if kind == .Integer { /* format int */ }

features.name: @thread_local
features.what_it_does: Storage class attribute. Declares a global variable with thread-local storage (TLS). Each thread gets its own copy. Compiler may skip TLS on some platforms (e.g., Windows i386).
features.telemetry_use: Store per-thread telemetry buffers, frame counters, or ring buffers without synchronization overhead. Each thread appends to its own buffer; flush on demand.
features.example: @thread_local telemetry_buffer: [dynamic]Telemetry_Event

features.name: debug_trap
features.what_it_does: Emit CPU debug trap instruction (SIGTRAP on Unix, breakpoint on Windows). If running under debugger, breaks into debugger; otherwise raises signal.
features.telemetry_use: Conditional breakpoint on telemetry anomalies: if value exceeds threshold, call debug_trap() to halt for inspection. Compile-time disableable.
features.example: if frame_time > 16ms { intrinsics.debug_trap() }  // break if frame drop

features.name: ODIN_DEBUG
features.syntax: ODIN_DEBUG :: ODIN_DEBUG  // true if -debug flag passed
features.what_it_does: Compile-time constant set by -debug compiler flag. Enables debug info generation (DWARF, PDB, etc.). Can be tested in #when directives.
features.telemetry_use: Conditionally enable expensive telemetry: `when ODIN_DEBUG { instrument = true }` to disable overhead in release builds.
features.example: when ODIN_DEBUG { TELEMETRY_ENABLED :: true } else { TELEMETRY_ENABLED :: false }

features.name: ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT
features.syntax: ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT :: ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT  // true if -disable-assert flag passed
features.what_it_does: Compile-time constant. If true, all assert() calls are elided at compile time (no code generated).
features.telemetry_use: Pair with custom assertion handler: assertions become high-performance telemetry checkpoints in debug mode, zero cost in release.
features.example: when !ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT { assert(value > 0, loc=#caller_location) } else { /* no code */ }

features.name: Spall context
features.syntax: spall.context_create :: proc(filename: string, sleep := 2 * time.Second) -> (ctx: spall.Context, ok: bool) #optional_ok
features.what_it_does: Open a Spall trace file for event logging. Measures TSC frequency via sleep, initializes stream header with calibrated timestamp scale. Part of core/prof/spall profiling package.
features.telemetry_use: Initialize Spall profiler output file on startup. Spall is a high-performance event tracer (compatible with speedscope). Use to record per-frame events.
features.example: spall_ctx, ok := spall.context_create("trace.spall", time.Second); defer spall.context_destroy(&spall_ctx)

features.name: Spall buffer
features.syntax: spall.buffer_create :: proc(data: []byte, tid: u32 = 0, pid: u32 = 0) -> (buffer: spall.Buffer, ok: bool) #optional_ok
features.what_it_does: Allocate a per-thread buffer for Spall events. Data slice must be ≥1024 bytes. tid/pid are optional thread/process IDs for multi-threaded traces.
features.telemetry_use: Create one Spall buffer per thread (use @thread_local). Append Begin/End events to log scope entries/exits. Flush periodically with spall.buffer_flush.
features.example: @thread_local spall_buf: spall.Buffer; spall_buf, _ = spall.buffer_create(alloc_data[:])

features.name: Benchmark_Options
features.syntax: Benchmark_Options :: struct { setup: #type proc(...), bench: #type proc(...), teardown: #type proc(...), rounds: int, bytes: int, input: []u8, count: int, processed: int, output: []u8, hash: u128, duration: Duration, rounds_per_second: f64, megabytes_per_second: f64, user_data: rawptr }
features.what_it_does: Configuration for time.benchmark() harness. Captures setup/bench/teardown procedures, measures elapsed duration, and computes throughput (rounds/sec, MB/sec).
features.telemetry_use: Benchmark code paths and record throughput metrics as telemetry. Replay benchmarks periodically (per frame, per session) to track performance regressions.
features.example: opts := time.Benchmark_Options{bench=my_bench}; time.benchmark(&opts); telem.record("throughput_mb_s", opts.megabytes_per_second)

features.name: Level (enum)
features.what_it_does: Severity level hierarchy for log messages: Debug=0, Info=10, Warning=20, Error=30, Fatal=40. Numeric gaps allow custom levels in-between.
features.telemetry_use: Filter which messages are recorded (e.g., only Error+ in production). Enables hierarchical importance tracking of observed events.
features.example: if event_level >= context.logger.lowest_level { ... }

features.name: Option (enum)
features.what_it_does: Bit flags controlling log message formatting: Level, Date, Time, Short_File_Path, Long_File_Path, Line, Procedure, Terminal_Color, Thread_Id.
features.telemetry_use: Configure which metadata is stamped on each message. Enable/disable location info, timestamps, thread IDs, colors per logger.
features.example: Options{ .Date, .Time, .Short_File_Path, .Line, .Procedure }

features.name: Source_Code_Location (struct)
features.what_it_does: Struct capturing call site: file_path (string), line (i32), column (i32), procedure (string). Populated by #caller_location built-in.
features.telemetry_use: Attach call-site metadata to every log entry: where in code the event occurred, which function. Zero-cost when stamped via #caller_location.
features.example: location := #caller_location; // Captures log.odin:188:debug()
features.syntax: Source_Code_Location :: struct { file_path: string, line, column: i32, procedure: string }

features.name: Logger (struct)
features.what_it_does: Opaque handle binding a logger procedure, data pointer, lowest_level threshold, and formatting options. Stored in context.logger.
features.telemetry_use: Central dispatch point for all observability: one Logger per context can multiplex to file, console, network, or custom backends.
features.example: context.logger = create_console_logger(Level.Info)
features.syntax: Logger :: struct { procedure: Logger_Proc, data: rawptr, lowest_level: Level, options: Options }

features.name: Logger_Proc (function type)
features.what_it_does: Callback signature: (data: rawptr, level: Level, text: string, options: Options, location: Source_Code_Location)
features.telemetry_use: Define custom observability backends (e.g., ring buffer, structured JSON, remote telemetry sink). Invoked on every log call.
features.example: my_logger_proc :: proc(data: rawptr, level: Level, text: string, options: Options, location := #caller_location) { /* write to ring buffer */ }
features.syntax: Logger_Proc :: #type proc(data: rawptr, level: Level_Level, text: string, options: Logger_Options, location := #caller_location)

features.name: log() / logf()
features.what_it_does: Core logging dispatch: formats message (log uses fmt.tprint, logf uses fmt.tprintf), checks level threshold, invokes logger.procedure with location metadata.
features.telemetry_use: Entry point for all event recording. Automatic level filtering + location stamping. logf enables formatted output (e.g., values at call site).
features.example: log(.Info, "event", value, location=#caller_location); logf(.Warning, "error: %v", err, location=#caller_location)
features.syntax:
log :: proc(level: Level, args: ..any, sep := " ", location := #caller_location)
logf :: proc(level: Level, fmt_str: string, args: ..any, location := #caller_location)

features.name: debug() / info() / warn() / error() / fatal()
features.what_it_does: Convenience level-specific log wrappers. Identical to log() but with level pre-set.
features.telemetry_use: Semantic level names reduce mistakes; code readability for observability intent. fatal() calls runtime.panic().
features.example: debug("entered loop"); error("connection failed", err)

features.name: debugf() / infof() / warnf() / errorf() / fatalf()
features.what_it_does: Format string versions of level-specific logs. Use fmt.tprintf internally.
features.telemetry_use: Capture formatted values in telemetry (e.g., debugf("x=%d y=%d", x, y)). Reduces string allocations vs manual fmt + log.
features.example: infof("frame %d fps=%f", frame_num, fps)

features.name: #caller_location (built-in directive)
features.what_it_does: Compiler directive: captures file_path, line, column, procedure name of the call site and inlines as a Source_Code_Location literal.
features.telemetry_use: Zero-cost automatic location stamping on every log. Enable post-mortem analysis of where events occurred without manual tracking.
features.example: log(.Info, msg, location=#caller_location) → passes {file_path: "main.odin", line: 42, procedure: "main"}

features.name: create_console_logger()
features.what_it_does: Factory: builds Logger bound to stdout/stderr. Routes level < Error to stdout, Error+ to stderr. Respects Terminal_Color option.
features.telemetry_use: Default observability backend. Enables ANSI coloring (debug=dark grey, info=reset, warn=yellow, error/fatal=red). Configurable metadata (date, time, location, thread ID).
features.example: context.logger = create_console_logger(Level.Debug, Default_Console_Logger_Opts | {.Thread_Id})
features.syntax: create_console_logger :: proc(lowest := Level.Debug, opt := Default_Console_Logger_Opts, ident := "", allocator := context.allocator) -> Logger

features.name: create_file_logger()
features.what_it_does: Factory: builds Logger bound to file handle. Routes all messages to the same file (no stderr split).
features.telemetry_use: Persistent event log. Can combine with multi_logger for simultaneous console + file telemetry. Ident parameter adds a prefix per message.
features.example: f := os.open("game.log", os.O_CREATE | os.O_WRONLY); flog := create_file_logger(f, Level.Debug, ..., ident="GAME")
features.syntax: create_file_logger :: proc(f: ^os.File, lowest := Level.Debug, opt := Default_File_Logger_Opts, ident := "", allocator := context.allocator) -> Logger

features.name: destroy_console_logger() / destroy_file_logger()
features.what_it_does: Cleanup: deallocate logger data and optionally close file handle.
features.telemetry_use: Ensure file handles are flushed and closed when shutting down observability.
features.example: destroy_file_logger(context.logger)
features.syntax: destroy_console_logger / destroy_file_logger :: proc(log: Logger, allocator := context.allocator)

features.name: create_multi_logger()
features.what_it_does: Factory: chains multiple Loggers. Each log call is broadcast to all child loggers (respecting each child's lowest_level).
features.telemetry_use: Send telemetry to multiple sinks simultaneously (console + file + network, etc.). Enables hierarchical filtering per sink.
features.example: multi := create_multi_logger(console_log, file_log, network_log); context.logger = multi

features.name: destroy_multi_logger()
features.what_it_does: Cleanup: deallocate multi-logger's child list (does NOT destroy children — caller must do that).
features.telemetry_use: Reclaim memory when tearing down multi-logger, but maintain child logger independence.
features.example: destroy_multi_logger(context.logger)

features.name: Log_Allocator (struct + log_allocator_init() + log_allocator())
features.what_it_does: Wrapping allocator that logs every alloc/free/resize call via context.logger. Respects level threshold and formats size as Bytes or Human (KiB, MiB, etc).
features.telemetry_use: Automatic memory observability: capture all allocation patterns, detect leaks, profile heap behavior without manual instrumentation. Thread-safe (mutex-protected).

features.name: nil_logger() / nil_logger_proc()

features.telemetry_use: Zero-overhead telemetry disable: set context.logger to nil_logger in production builds to eliminate logging cost (no allocation, no formatting, no I/O).

features.name: Default_Console_Logger_Opts / Default_File_Logger_Opts

features.name: Full_Timestamp_Opts / Location_Header_Opts

features.what_it_does: Log at Fatal level and then unconditionally panic.
features.telemetry_use: Unrecoverable error telemetry: last event before crash is in log stream.

features.what_it_does: CPU TSC (time stamp counter) support detection and frequency query. Used for high-resolution cycle counting on x86/ARM.

features.name: register_user_formatter
features.what_it_does: Registers a custom format handler for a specific type. Maps typeid to User_Formatter proc. Must call set_user_formatters() first to initialize global _user_formatters map. Returns error if formatter already registered or map not initialized.
features.telemetry_use: Zero-overhead instrumentation: custom formatters intercept format calls for application types without changing call sites. Enables domain-specific serialization (encode values as JSON, protobuf, custom binary) at observation points.

features.syntax: User_Formatter :: #type proc(fi: ^Info, arg: any, verb: rune) -> bool
features.what_it_does: Callback type for custom format handlers. Receives Info struct (containing writer, flags like fi.hash, fi.width), the value as 'any', and the format verb (rune). Returns true if formatting succeeded, false to fall through to default (bad verb error).
features.telemetry_use: Pluggable serialization layer: intercepts all fmt calls for a type, enabling custom telemetry backends (emit to tracing, metrics, event logs, structured formats). fi.hash flag indicates deep vs. shallow format requests.
features.example: MyFormatter :: proc(fi: ^fmt.Info, arg: any, verb: rune) -> bool { switch verb { case 'v', 'd': fmt.fmt_int(fi, u64(cast(^MyType)arg.data).value, true, 64, verb); return true; case: return false } }

features.what_it_does: Initializes the global _user_formatters map. Must be called once at startup before register_user_formatter. Asserts if called more than once.
features.telemetry_use: Initialization hook for telemetry instrumentation. Centralizes formatter registration at program startup, enabling feature-flag-based conditional formatters (dev vs. prod observability).
features.example: main :: proc() { fmt.set_user_formatters(new(map[typeid]fmt.User_Formatter)); fmt.register_user_formatter(...); }

features.what_it_does: Formats into a new heap-allocated string using provided allocator. Returns formatted string; caller must free. Supports all verbs.
features.telemetry_use: Buffer accumulation: format telemetry events into strings, batch them, then flush to persistent storage. Enables time-windowed telemetry collection.

features.what_it_does: Formats into string using context.temp_allocator. Auto-freed at end of frame/scope. Low overhead for per-frame telemetry.
features.telemetry_use: Per-frame telemetry: capture state snapshots every frame without allocator churn. Ideal for game loop instrumentation and frame-synchronized sampling.

features.what_it_does: Formats into pre-allocated byte buffer. No allocation; writes up to buffer capacity. Returns substring of buffer with formatted content.
features.telemetry_use: Zero-alloc telemetry: ring buffers for continuous event logging, fixed-size telemetry packets, embedded systems. Enables deterministic memory usage in observers.
features.example: buf := make([]byte, 256); snapshot := fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "%v at %p\n", value, &value); telemetry_write(snapshot);

features.name: Tracking_Allocator
features.what_it_does: A wrapper allocator that intercepts all allocation/free/resize operations on a backing allocator and maintains a live map of all current allocations with their metadata (pointer, size, alignment, call site) and aggregate statistics (total allocated, total freed, current/peak memory). On attempted bad-free (freeing a pointer not in the map), invokes a callback (default: crash with location; alternative: record in array). Mutex-protected for thread safety.
features.telemetry_use: Comprehensive memory telemetry: capture every allocation event (via Tracking_Allocator_Entry) with exact call site (Source_Code_Location: file, line, column, procedure name), query current live allocations at any time, track memory growth over time via current_memory_allocated/peak_memory_allocated fields, detect leaks by scanning allocation_map at program end, catch double-frees and invalid frees. All metadata is deterministic (call sites + sizes); totals accumulate deterministically across runs.
features.syntax: struct { backing: Allocator; allocation_map: map[rawptr]Tracking_Allocator_Entry; bad_free_callback: Tracking_Allocator_Bad_Free_Callback; bad_free_array: [dynamic]Tracking_Allocator_Bad_Free_Entry; mutex: sync.Mutex; clear_on_free_all: bool; total_memory_allocated: i64; total_allocation_count: i64; total_memory_freed: i64; total_free_count: i64; peak_memory_allocated: i64; current_memory_allocated: i64; }

features.name: Tracking_Allocator_Entry

features.telemetry_use: Per-allocation metadata capture for precise instrumentation: store (pointer -> Entry) in the tracking map to reconstruct full allocation history, map Source_Code_Location to identify which code paths allocate most memory, compute totals/averages by location or mode. The location field provides zero-overhead-when-disabled: if tracking is disabled, no entry is created; if enabled, location is captured at call site via #caller_location.

entry := track.allocation_map[some_ptr]
fmt.printf("Allocated %v bytes at %s:%v:%v in %s()\n", entry.size, entry.location.file_path, entry.location.line, entry.location.column, entry.location.procedure)

features.name: Mutex_Allocator
features.what_it_does: A simple thread-safe wrapper around any allocator. Serializes all allocator requests (alloc, free, resize, etc.) via a sync.Mutex, ensuring only one thread can perform an allocation at a time on the wrapped backing allocator.
features.telemetry_use: Thread-safe memory observability: combine Mutex_Allocator with Tracking_Allocator to instrument multi-threaded programs without data races. The mutex ensures allocation_map, totals, and peak tracking are updated atomically. Enables heap profiling in concurrent code.

mem.mutex_allocator_init(&mutex_wrap, mem.tracking_allocator(&track))
context.allocator = mem.mutex_allocator(&mutex_wrap)
// Now multi-threaded allocations are serialized and tracked

features.name: Allocator_Mode enum (Alloc, Alloc_Non_Zeroed, Free, Free_All, Resize, Resize_Non_Zeroed, Query_Features, Query_Info)
features.what_it_does: Discriminates the type of allocator operation. Each value triggers different behavior in an allocator_proc: Alloc/Alloc_Non_Zeroed allocate, Free frees a pointer, Free_All frees all, Resize reallocates, Query_Features queries supported modes, Query_Info queries size/alignment of a live allocation.
features.telemetry_use: Operation-level telemetry: allocator wrappers can branch on mode to implement per-operation-type instrumentation (e.g., count Alloc vs Free vs Resize separately, time each mode). Tracking_Allocator uses mode to dispatch to track_alloc or track_free and update corresponding counters.
features.syntax: Allocator_Mode :: enum byte { Alloc, Free, Free_All, Resize, Query_Features, Query_Info, Alloc_Non_Zeroed, Resize_Non_Zeroed }

features.name: query_info (allocator intrinsic)
features.what_it_does: Queries a live allocator for information about a specific pointer: returns an Allocator_Query_Info struct with the pointer, size (if tracked), and alignment. Dispatches to the allocator's procedure with mode=Query_Info. Some allocators (like Tracking_Allocator) support it; others may not.
features.telemetry_use: On-demand size/alignment lookup for a pointer: if you have a pointer and need to know how many bytes were allocated, call query_info() to extract size and alignment without maintaining a separate map. Tracking_Allocator populates this from its allocation_map.
features.syntax:
query_info(pointer: rawptr, allocator: Allocator, loc := #caller_location) -> (props: Allocator_Query_Info)
Allocator_Query_Info :: struct { pointer: rawptr; size: Maybe(int); alignment: Maybe(int); }

features.name: now
features.what_it_does: Captures wall-clock time (Unix epoch timestamp in nanoseconds). Uses OS-specific wall-clock: CLOCK_REALTIME on Unix/Linux, GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime on Windows.
features.telemetry_use: Record absolute timestamp for events. Useful for correlating with external logs or wall-clock progression. Insufficient for measuring durations due to system clock adjustments (NTP).
features.example: t := time.now(); fmt.println(time.time_to_unix_nano(t))
features.source_ref: core:time/time.odin:120, platform implementations in core:time/time_unix.odin, core:time/time_windows.odin, core:time/time_linux.odin

features.name: tick_now
features.what_it_does: Captures monotonic time (relative, never goes backward). Uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW on macOS/Linux, QueryPerformanceCounter on Windows. Immune to wall-clock adjustments.
features.telemetry_use: TELEMETRY PRIMARY: measure elapsed time between events, sample times in frame loops, duration tracking for per-frame metrics. Essential for observing performance without clock skew artifacts.
features.example: start := time.tick_now(); ...; elapsed := time.tick_since(start)
features.source_ref: core:time/perf.odin:17, platform implementations in core:time/time_unix.odin:41, core:time/time_windows.odin:26, core:time/time_linux.odin:30

features.name: tick_since
features.what_it_does: Returns elapsed Duration since a captured Tick. Computes tick_diff(start, tick_now()), safe for repeated calls.
features.telemetry_use: Query elapsed time without explicit tick capture. Canonical for 'how much time since event X'. Forms basis of per-frame delta-time and per-scope durations.
features.example: d := time.tick_since(frame_start)

features.name: tick_diff
features.what_it_does: Computes Duration between two captured Ticks. Subtracts internal nanosecond counters, result is deterministic given two fixed Ticks.
features.telemetry_use: Capture two ticks at known scope boundaries, compute exact elapsed time. Lower-level than tick_since; enables latency histograms and event windowing.
features.example: t1 := time.tick_now(); ...; t2 := time.tick_now(); d := time.tick_diff(t1, t2)

features.name: tick_lap_time
features.what_it_does: Returns Duration since last call, updates prev to current tick. On first call (zero-init prev), returns 0. Maintains lap state in caller's storage.
features.telemetry_use: Per-frame or per-event delta-time without manual tick tracking. Stateful alternative to tick_since; compact for streaming telemetry (e.g., frame-to-frame elapsed in a loop).
features.example: var lap time.Tick; for { delta := time.tick_lap_time(&lap); telemetry.log_frame_delta(delta) }

features.name: read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: Reads CPU TSC (Time Stamp Counter). Raw x86/ARM cycle count. Deterministic on same CPU core if invariant TSC is present; varies across cores and CPU frequency states on older hardware.
features.telemetry_use: Ultra-fine-grained timing: measure nanosecond-scale latencies within a loop, profile CPU-cycle budget per instruction stream, detect stalls. Requires conversion to wall time via tsc_frequency. Zero-overhead sampling when disabled in telemetry config.
features.example: c1 := time.read_cycle_counter(); ...; c2 := time.read_cycle_counter(); cycles := c2 - c1

features.name: read_cycle_counter_frequency
features.what_it_does: Returns CPU cycle frequency in Hz (e.g., 3_600_000_000 for 3.6 GHz). Obtained from runtime or as fallback computed measurement.
features.telemetry_use: Convert raw cycle counts to wall time: ns = cycles * 1e9 / frequency. Enables telemetry pipelines to translate TSC deltas into milliseconds or seconds.
features.example: freq := time.read_cycle_counter_frequency(); ns := (c2 - c1) * 1e9 / freq

features.name: tsc_frequency
features.what_it_does: Obtains CPU's invariant TSC frequency. Checks has_invariant_tsc(), queries OS, falls back to sleeping and timing TSC delta. Returns (hz, ok).
features.telemetry_use: Calibrate cycle-to-nanosecond conversion at runtime. Essential for cross-CPU telemetry stacks that record TSC. Failure (ok=false) indicates CPU lacks invariant TSC and cycle counts are unreliable.
features.example: hz, ok := time.tsc_frequency(); if ok { telemetry.set_tsc_hz(hz) }

features.name: has_invariant_tsc
features.what_it_does: Checks via CPUID (x86) or returns true (ARM64) whether CPU supports invariant TSC. Invariant TSC runs at fixed frequency independent of ACPI/turbo.
features.telemetry_use: Gating feature: only sample TSC in telemetry if invariant TSC is present. Avoids collecting unreliable cycle counts on older processors.
features.example: if time.has_invariant_tsc() { telemetry.enable_tsc_sampling() }

features.name: Stopwatch
features.syntax: Stopwatch :: struct { running: bool, _start_time: Tick, _accumulation: Duration }
features.what_it_does: Accumulates total elapsed time across multiple start/stop cycles. Tracks running state, start Tick, and accumulated Duration independently. Used for multi-segment timing (e.g., total game-loop time across frames).
features.telemetry_use: Aggregate per-frame or per-phase times into a running total. Enables telemetry of 'total time in subsystem X' across frame window without allocating a histogram. Thread-local instances per profiling domain.
features.example: var sw time.Stopwatch; time.stopwatch_start(&sw); ...; time.stopwatch_stop(&sw); total := time.stopwatch_duration(sw)

features.name: stopwatch_start
features.what_it_does: Begins timing a stopwatch. Captures tick_now(), sets running=true. Idempotent (ignores if already running).
features.telemetry_use: Mark entry to a profiled region. Pairs with stopwatch_stop to measure wall time.
features.example: time.stopwatch_start(&my_stopwatch)

features.name: stopwatch_stop
features.what_it_does: Ends timing. Accumulates tick_diff(start, now) into _accumulation. Sets running=false. Idempotent.
features.telemetry_use: Mark exit from profiled region. Enables hierarchical or nested measurements without re-allocating structures.
features.example: time.stopwatch_stop(&my_stopwatch)

features.name: stopwatch_duration
features.what_it_does: Returns total accumulated time. If still running, includes elapsed since last start. Non-mutating.
features.telemetry_use: Query total so far without stopping. Allows telemetry snapshot queries during an ongoing measurement.
features.example: elapsed := time.stopwatch_duration(sw); telemetry.sample_frame_time(elapsed)

features.name: stopwatch_reset
features.what_it_does: Clears accumulated time and stops if running. Resets to zero-initialized state.
features.telemetry_use: Clear per-frame telemetry counters at frame boundary (e.g., reset frame-time accumulator on new frame).
features.example: time.stopwatch_reset(&frame_timer)

features.name: SCOPED_TICK_DURATION
features.what_it_does: Deferred macro: captures tick at scope entry, computes and stores elapsed Duration to *d at scope exit via deferred call. Zero-cost abstraction for scope timing.
features.telemetry_use: TELEMETRY ZERO-OVERHEAD: inline scope measurement without manual tick calls. Patterns: { SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&frame_time); ... } or { SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&hot_path_ns); critical_code(); }. Duration written only on exit.
features.example: { SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&inner_scope_time); hot_inner_loop(); } // inner_scope_time now contains elapsed

features.name: Duration
features.what_it_does: Strongly typed i64 nanosecond count. Arithmetic with Duration preserves type. Constants: Nanosecond, Microsecond, Millisecond, Second, Minute, Hour.
features.telemetry_use: Type-safe representation of elapsed time for all measurements. Supports conversion to f64 seconds via duration_seconds(), milliseconds via duration_milliseconds(), etc.
features.example: d: Duration; d = 5 * time.Millisecond; fmt.println(time.duration_seconds(d))

features.name: duration_nanoseconds
features.what_it_does: Extract raw nanosecond count (i64).
features.telemetry_use: Store telemetry as raw ns for lossless quantization. Useful for histogram buckets (e.g., [0..1000ns], [1000..10000ns]).
features.example: ns := time.duration_nanoseconds(frame_elapsed); telemetry.histogram_add(frame_ns_histogram, ns)

features.name: duration_seconds
features.what_it_does: Convert Duration to floating-point seconds.
features.telemetry_use: Human-readable telemetry export (logs, dashboards). Enables fractional seconds for slow operations (e.g., asset load time = 2.345 seconds).
features.example: secs := time.duration_seconds(op_time); fmt.printf("op took %.3f seconds", secs)

features.name: duration_milliseconds
features.what_it_does: Convert Duration to milliseconds (f64).
features.telemetry_use: Frame-time telemetry in typical game loop format (e.g., frame_time_ms = 16.667 for 60 FPS).
features.example: ms := time.duration_milliseconds(frame_time); telemetry.log_frame_duration_ms(ms)

features.name: diff
features.what_it_does: Computes Duration between two wall-clock Times (Unix timestamps). NOT recommended for elapsed-time measurement (susceptible to NTP adjustments).
features.telemetry_use: Correlate events via wall-clock timestamps (e.g., event A at 10:05:03.100, event B at 10:05:05.200, diff=2.1s). Use tick_diff for precise elapsed time.
features.example: event_duration := time.diff(event_start_time, event_end_time)

features.name: since
features.what_it_does: Computes Duration from a wall-clock Time to now(). Equivalent to diff(start, now()). Subject to wall-clock changes.
features.telemetry_use: Wall-clock elapsed time for event correlation (e.g., seconds since app start). NOT for frame timing; use tick_since instead.
features.example: app_uptime := time.since(startup_wallclock_time)

features.name: Benchmark_Options
features.syntax: Benchmark_Options :: struct { setup, bench, teardown, rounds, bytes, input, count, processed, output, hash, duration, rounds_per_second, megabytes_per_second, user_data }
features.what_it_does: Configuration for benchmark() harness. Callbacks for setup, benchmark, teardown. Output fields: duration, rounds_per_second, megabytes_per_second.
features.telemetry_use: Structured benchmarking framework. Telemetry use: record multiple runs with variants (flags, #config), capture duration per iteration, compute throughput (elements/sec, MB/sec). Integrates with claim verification (tools/substrate/claim.py).
features.example: opts := time.Benchmark_Options{ bench = my_bench_fn }; time.benchmark(&opts)

features.name: benchmark
features.what_it_does: Runs harness: calls setup, times bench via SCOPED_TICK_DURATION, calls teardown. Fills Benchmark_Options with duration, rounds_per_second, megabytes_per_second.
features.telemetry_use: TELEMETRY HARNESS: benchmark suite for continuous integration. Pairs with claim verification to assert 'faster k' (speedup requirement), detect regressions. Output fields are telemetry metrics.
features.example: time.benchmark(&bench_opts); fmt.printf("%.2f ops/sec", bench_opts.rounds_per_second)

features.name: x86_cpuid
features.syntax: x86_cpuid :: proc(ax, cx: u32) -> (eax, ebx, ecx, edx: u32)
features.what_it_does: Execute x86 CPUID instruction. Queries CPU capabilities (leaf ax, subleaf cx). Returns register values.
features.telemetry_use: Detect CPU features for conditional telemetry (e.g., check invariant TSC via leaf 0x80000007). Used internally by has_invariant_tsc().
features.example: eax, _, _, edx := intrinsics.x86_cpuid(0x80_000_007, 0); has_inv_tsc := (edx & (1 << 8)) != 0

features.name: Time
features.syntax: Time :: struct { _nsec: i64 }  // Unix epoch nanoseconds
features.what_it_does: Absolute time value (Unix epoch, nanosecond precision). Range: 1677-09-21 to 2262-04-11. Obtained via now().
