features.telemetry_use: Store absolute timestamps for event logs. Enables replay, external correlation, real-time telemetry ingestion to backend (convert to Unix seconds or RFC3339 for JSON).
features.example: t := time.now(); unix_ns := time.time_to_unix_nano(t)

features.name: Tick
features.what_it_does: Monotonic time value (relative, never decreases). Internal representation: nanosecond offset from arbitrary epoch. Opaque; only meaningful for diff/since operations.
features.telemetry_use: TELEMETRY PRIMARY: represent captured timepoints for deterministic elapsed-time measurements. Thread-safe when used with per-thread tick_now() calls.
features.example: var tick_list [100]time.Tick; for i in 0..<100 { tick_list[i] = time.tick_now() }

features.name: time_to_unix_nano
features.what_it_does: Extract raw Unix timestamp in nanoseconds from a Time.
features.telemetry_use: Serialize absolute timestamp to telemetry backend. Enables cross-system correlation (compare with timestamps from other services).
features.example: ns := time.time_to_unix_nano(event_time); backend.log(event_name, ns)

features.name: time_to_unix
features.what_it_does: Extract Unix timestamp in seconds (integer division by 1e9).
features.telemetry_use: Coarse-grained timestamps for telemetry indexing by second granularity (e.g., aggregate frame times by second).
features.example: sec := time.time_to_unix(t); day_index := sec / (24 * 3600)

features.name: debug/trace.Context
features.what_it_does: Opaque stack trace context that manages symbol resolution for captured call stacks. Platform-specific (Windows uses Dbghelp, Linux/Darwin uses libbacktrace/dladdr). Requires -debug compiler flag.
features.telemetry_use: Initialize once per program to enable stack trace capture and symbol resolution as telemetry data. Essential prerequisite for converting raw frame addresses to human-readable file/line/procedure names.

features.name: debug/trace.frames
features.what_it_does: Captures current call stack as an array of Frame (uintptr). Takes skip count to exclude caller frames. Uses RtlCaptureStackBackTrace on Windows or libbacktrace on Linux/Darwin.
features.telemetry_use: Snapshot the call stack at any point in program execution (e.g., on error, at sampling time, before state change). Returns raw addresses suitable for lazy symbol resolution.

features.name: debug/trace.Frame
features.what_it_does: Distinct uintptr representing a single stack frame's return address. Used as opaque handle; must be passed to resolve() to get file/line/procedure.
features.telemetry_use: Store raw frame addresses compactly (8 bytes each) in telemetry buffer; resolve to names on-demand or during analysis phase to control memory/CPU cost.
features.example:
frame: trace.Frame = <captured from frames()>
fl := trace.resolve(&ctx, frame, allocator)

features.name: debug/trace.resolve
features.what_it_does: Converts a Frame address to Frame_Location (file_path, line, column, procedure). Allocates strings; thread-safe via atomic in_resolve flag on Windows (SRWLOCK). Cost: symbol lookups via OS debug info (expensive).
features.telemetry_use: Transform captured frame addresses into symbolic telemetry on-demand. Typically batched post-capture or during off-line analysis to avoid blocking hot paths. Deterministic given same binary + address space layout.
features.syntax: resolve :: proc(ctx: ^Context, frame: Frame, allocator: runtime.Allocator) -> (result: Frame_Location)
features.example:
fl := trace.resolve(&ctx, frame, context.temp_allocator)
runtime.print_caller_location(fl.loc)
defer trace.delete_frame_location(fl)

features.name: debug/trace.Frame_Location
features.what_it_does: Struct holding resolved frame metadata: Source_Code_Location (file_path, line, column, procedure) + allocator handle. Allocated strings must be freed via delete_frame_location().
features.telemetry_use: Store resolved stack frame metadata in telemetry records. Includes file path, line number, column, and procedure name—all useful for pinpointing execution context.
features.syntax: Frame_Location :: struct { using loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location, allocator: runtime.Allocator }
features.example:
fl: trace.Frame_Location = trace.resolve(&ctx, frame, alloc)
print(fl.file_path, fl.line, fl.procedure)

features.name: runtime.Source_Code_Location
features.what_it_does: Struct capturing source code metadata: file_path (string), line (i32), column (i32), procedure (string). Filled by #caller_location built-in or by trace.resolve().
features.telemetry_use: Core telemetry datum for recording where in source code an observation occurred. Cheap to capture (via #caller_location); expensive to resolve from raw addresses (via trace.resolve).
features.syntax: Source_Code_Location :: struct { file_path, procedure: string, line, column: i32 }
features.example:
loc := #caller_location
runtime.print_caller_location(loc)

features.name: #caller_location
features.what_it_does: Compile-time directive that yields Source_Code_Location of call site (file_path, line, column, procedure). Zero-overhead; resolved at compile time.
features.telemetry_use: Lightweight telemetry marker—capture calling location in log messages, assertions, error handlers without runtime cost. Used pervasively in context.logger callbacks and assertions.
features.example: proc my_error(msg: string, loc := #caller_location) { ... }

features.name: runtime.print_caller_location
features.what_it_does: Prints Source_Code_Location to stderr in format: file(line:column) or file:line:column depending on ODIN_ERROR_POS_STYLE. Contextless; no allocation.
features.telemetry_use: Dump location metadata to stderr/telemetry log. Often used in assertion/panic handlers. Zero allocation, safe to call from signal handlers.
features.example: runtime.print_caller_location(loc)

features.name: runtime.write_caller_location
features.what_it_does: Writes Source_Code_Location to a byte buffer (in-place, no allocation) with the same format as print_caller_location. Returns bool indicating success (buffer full = false).
features.telemetry_use: Serialize location metadata into fixed-size telemetry record or buffer without allocation. Suitable for lockless telemetry rings or embedded systems.
features.syntax: write_caller_location :: proc "contextless" (i: ^int, buf: []byte, loc: Source_Code_Location) -> bool
features.example:
offset: int
write_caller_location(&offset, buffer[:], loc)
telemetry_submit(buffer[:offset])

features.name: log.debug / log.info / log.warn / log.error / log.fatal
features.what_it_does: Structured logging procs with automatic location capture. Each takes variadic args, separator, and optional location parameter. Delegates to context.logger callback.
features.telemetry_use: Structured log-based telemetry—each call automatically captures file/line/procedure and log level. Integrates with context.logger for centralized observability pipeline.
features.example:
import "core:log"
log.info("state changed", value, location=#caller_location)

features.name: runtime.Logger
features.what_it_does: Struct holding a Logger_Proc callback + data ptr + lowest_level + options. Pluggable logging backend. Installed in context.logger; context.logger.procedure is called by log.* procs.
features.telemetry_use: Central observability hook—write a custom Logger_Proc to capture all structured logs with automatic location + level + timestamp. Can serialize to file, buffer, network, etc.
features.syntax: Logger :: struct { procedure: Logger_Proc, data: rawptr, lowest_level: Logger_Level, options: Logger_Options }
features.example: context.logger = log.Logger{ ... custom_logger_proc ... }

features.name: runtime.Logger_Level
features.what_it_does: Enum with levels Debug=0, Info=10, Warning=20, Error=30, Fatal=40. Used for log filtering and severity classification.
features.telemetry_use: Tag telemetry events by severity (debug, info, warning, error, fatal). Allows filtering and alerting on high-severity events.
features.syntax: Logger_Level :: enum uint { Debug=0, Info=10, Warning=20, Error=30, Fatal=40 }
features.example: if level >= log.Level.Error { ... alert ... }

features.name: runtime.Logger_Option / Logger_Options
features.what_it_does: Bit set of metadata flags: Level, Date, Time, Short_File_Path, Long_File_Path, Line, Procedure, Terminal_Color, Thread_Id. Tells logger which metadata to attach to each log.
features.telemetry_use: Configure which telemetry metadata to capture per-log event. E.g., .Level | .Time | .Procedure for lightweight observability.
features.syntax:
Logger_Option :: enum { Level, Date, Time, Short_File_Path, Long_File_Path, Line, Procedure, Terminal_Color, Thread_Id }
Logger_Options :: bit_set[Logger_Option]
features.example: opts := Logger_Options{ .Level, .Time, .Procedure }

features.name: time.Tick / tick_now / tick_diff / tick_since
features.what_it_does: Monotonic time primitives. Tick holds nanoseconds relative to unspecified epoch. tick_now() is O(1) on all platforms. tick_diff computes elapsed. tick_since is relative to now.
features.telemetry_use: Lightweight timestamp for every telemetry event (frame, log, sample). Monotonic (never goes backward), platform-optimized, nanosecond precision.
features.syntax:
tick_now :: proc "contextless" () -> Tick
tick_diff :: proc "contextless" (start, end: Tick) -> Duration
tick_since :: proc "contextless" (start: Tick) -> Duration
features.example:
start := time.tick_now()
... do work ...
elapsed := time.tick_since(start)
log.info(elapsed)

features.name: time.SCOPED_TICK_DURATION
features.what_it_does: Deferred in/out macro that automatically measures duration of a code block. Captures tick at entry, computes elapsed at exit via deferred callback.
features.telemetry_use: Zero-boilerplate scope timing—measure wall-clock time of any critical section or function. Defers automatically; duration written to Duration pointer.

features.name: intrinsics.read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: Read CPU cycle counter (TSC on x86, CNTVCT on ARM). Low-latency (<10 cycles), high-precision timing. Monotonic only if CPU has invariant TSC.
features.telemetry_use: Ultra-low-overhead cycle-accurate profiling. Capture cycle count alongside each telemetry event for detailed performance analysis. Avoid on CPUs without invariant TSC.
features.example:
cycles := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter()
... work ...
elapsed_cycles := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter() - cycles

features.name: time.has_invariant_tsc / tsc_frequency
features.what_it_does: Query whether CPU supports invariant TSC (time stamp counter). tsc_frequency() returns cycles/second if available; falls back to calibration via sleep if needed.
features.telemetry_use: Determine whether cycle-counter timing is reliable. If invariant TSC is present, safe to use read_cycle_counter for deterministic micro-benchmarking.
features.syntax:
has_invariant_tsc :: proc "contextless" () -> bool
tsc_frequency :: proc "contextless" (fallback_sleep := 2*Second) -> (u64, bool)
features.example: if time.has_invariant_tsc() { ... use cycles for timing ... }

features.name: runtime.Allocator / Allocator_Proc
features.what_it_does: Pluggable memory allocator interface. Proc receives allocator_data, mode (Allocate/Free/Resize), size, old_memory, and Source_Code_Location of call site. Returns allocated memory or error.
features.telemetry_use: Instrument allocator to track memory allocations per-frame or per-event. Allocator_Proc receives #caller_location automatically; can log file/line/proc for every allocation.
features.syntax:
Allocator_Proc :: #type proc(allocator_data: rawptr, mode: Allocator_Mode, size: int, old_memory: rawptr, old_size: int, location := #caller_location) -> ([]byte, Allocator_Error)
Allocator :: struct { procedure: Allocator_Proc, data: rawptr }

features.name: intrinsics.debug_trap
features.what_it_does: Software breakpoint / trap instruction. Halts execution and signals debugger (or OS if no debugger attached). Zero-overhead when not trapped.
features.telemetry_use: Conditional breakpoint at observability event (e.g., anomaly detection, failed assertion). Allows interactive inspection; skip in production.
features.example: if anomaly_detected { intrinsics.debug_trap() }

features.name: intrinsics.trap
features.what_it_does: Unconditional trap / panic instruction. Noreturn; terminates process immediately.
features.telemetry_use: Fail-safe shutdown on unrecoverable observability error (e.g., critical telemetry buffer overflow). Less common than debug_trap.
features.example: if critical_error { intrinsics.trap() }

features.name: time.Stopwatch / stopwatch_start / stopwatch_stop / stopwatch_duration
features.what_it_does: Stopwatch type + start/stop/reset/duration procs for measuring cumulative time across multiple intervals. Accumulates durations; doesn't lose time when paused.
features.telemetry_use: Track total wall-clock time spent in operation across many iterations/frames. Useful for per-frame telemetry aggregation.
features.example:
sw: time.Stopwatch
for frame in frames {
  time.stopwatch_start(&sw)
  ... frame work ...
  time.stopwatch_stop(&sw)
}
total := time.stopwatch_duration(sw)

features.name: time.benchmark / Benchmark_Options
features.what_it_does: Benchmark harness that runs a bench() proc and reports duration, rounds/sec, MB/sec. Supports setup/teardown. Designed for micro-benchmarking workloads.
features.telemetry_use: Batch benchmarking infrastructure—useful for per-frame performance regression detection. Outputs aggregated metrics (rounds_per_second, megabytes_per_second, duration).
features.syntax:
Benchmark_Options :: struct { setup, bench, teardown: proc(...), rounds, count, processed: int, duration: Duration, rounds_per_second, megabytes_per_second: f64, ... }
benchmark :: proc(options: ^Benchmark_Options, allocator := context.allocator) -> Benchmark_Error

features.name: runtime.Assertion_Failure_Proc / context.assertion_failure_proc
features.what_it_does: Custom assertion handler callback (noreturn). Called when assert/assertf fails. Receives message, location, and can call trace.frames() to log stack. Default calls runtime.trap().
features.telemetry_use: Hook to capture full stack trace + assertion message on failure. Install custom proc in context to log/analyze all assertion failures.
features.syntax:
Assertion_Failure_Proc :: #type proc(prefix, message: string, loc: Source_Code_Location) -> !
context.assertion_failure_proc = custom_handler

features.name: @(instrumentation_enter)
features.syntax:
@(instrumentation_enter)
procedure_name :: proc "contextless" (proc_address, call_site_return_address: rawptr, loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location)
features.what_it_does: Compiler-injected attribute that registers a callback fired automatically on EVERY procedure entry. The compiler inserts a call to this procedure at the start of every other proc (except those marked @(no_instrumentation)). Enables zero-manual-code telemetry for call tracking.
features.telemetry_use: Automatic call entry capture: log/trace every function call with its address, return site, and source location. No manual calls needed. Pairs with @(instrumentation_exit) for full call graphs and timing. Example: profiling frameworks like Spall use this to capture complete call traces for performance analysis.

features.name: @(instrumentation_exit)
features.syntax:
@(instrumentation_exit)
procedure_name :: proc "contextless" (proc_address, call_site_return_address: rawptr, loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location)
features.what_it_does: Compiler-injected attribute that registers a callback fired automatically on EVERY procedure exit (normal or abnormal). Fires before the return, capturing the proc's exit point. Mirrors @(instrumentation_enter) for symmetry.
features.telemetry_use: Automatic call exit capture: record when a function exits with its address and return site. Enables duration measurement (combined with enter hook), exception handling observation, resource cleanup tracking, and complete execution traces. Zero-overhead-when-disabled since hooks are compile-time conditional.

features.name: @(no_instrumentation)
features.what_it_does: Excludes a procedure from compiler-injected @(instrumentation_enter/exit) hooks. Prevents infinite recursion (e.g., the hooks themselves must not be instrumented) and reduces overhead for hot paths. Can be applied to any procedure.
features.telemetry_use: Prevents instrumentation overhead in telemetry infrastructure itself (profilers, loggers, error handlers). Marks procedures that are on the critical path of profiling. Used extensively in spall.odin for internal profiling buffers and error_checks.odin for bounds checking traps.

features.name: @(init)
features.what_it_does: Marks a procedure to be called automatically at program startup, before main() executes. Used for global state initialization. Called by the compiler-generated entry point if any @(init) procedures exist in the program.
features.telemetry_use: Initialize telemetry infrastructure at startup (e.g., open log files, set up profiling buffers, register signal handlers). Deterministic entry point for all observability setup. Terminal package uses it to configure color output and signal handling.

features.name: @(fini)
features.what_it_does: Marks a procedure to be called automatically at program shutdown, after main() returns. Mirror of @(init). Called in reverse order of their declaration.
features.telemetry_use: Flush and close telemetry streams at shutdown (e.g., finalize profiling output, close log files, dump remaining trace events). Ensures no data loss. Terminal package uses it to restore terminal state.

features.name: @(deferred_in)
features.what_it_does: Automatically calls exit_proc_name when the calling scope exits (like a guard/RAII). Enables lexically-scoped resource cleanup and measurement without explicit defer. The compiler inserts an implicit defer call.
features.telemetry_use: Scoped timing and event bracketing: mark entry/exit of a code region (e.g., frame, render pass, network request). @(deferred_out) pairs with exit proc. Used in spall.odin (SCOPED_EVENT), sync primitives (mutex lock/unlock), and temp allocators (arena begin/end).

features.name: @(deferred_out)
features.what_it_does: Pairs with @(deferred_in): when a procedure marked with this is called and returns, an implicit defer is inserted for the exit procedure with the return value as argument. Enables automatic resource release.
features.telemetry_use: Automatic exit-path instrumentation for scoped resources. Record return value and call exit hook. Combines with @(deferred_in) for paired enter/exit events. Enables event nesting and proper scope-stack management in profilers.

features.name: @(deferred_none)
features.what_it_does: Explicitly disables deferred cleanup even if the procedure type would otherwise support it. Used to opt out of automatic cleanup for performance-sensitive code where manual cleanup is safer.
features.telemetry_use: Skip deferred instrumentation for hot-path code (e.g., UI rendering in Orca, menu operations). Reduces call overhead when scope tracking is not needed or would impact frame time.
features.example:
@(deferred_none = ui_box_end)
ui_box :: proc(key: u64, flags: Ui_Flags = {}) -> ^Ui_Box

features.name: @(thread_local)
features.what_it_does: Allocates a variable with thread-local storage duration. Each thread gets its own independent copy. Initialized once per thread and persists for the thread's lifetime.
features.telemetry_use: Per-thread telemetry buffers and state (no synchronization needed). Example: Spall profiler maintains per-thread event buffers to avoid lock contention during trace capture. Chacha8 RNG also uses thread-local state.
features.example:
@(thread_local)
spall_buffer: spall.Buffer

features.name: @(static)
features.what_it_does: Marks a variable with static storage duration (global scope). Variable is initialized once at program start and persists for the entire program lifetime. Distinct from @(thread_local).
features.telemetry_use: Global telemetry state (e.g., profiler context, global counters, static event buffers). Zero initialization overhead after program startup. Not found in examples but is the default for module-level declarations.
features.example: spall_ctx: spall.Context  // implicitly @(static)

features.name: @(cold)
features.what_it_does: Hints to the compiler that this procedure is rarely executed (error paths, edge cases). Compiler moves the code out of the main instruction stream and deprioritizes branch prediction for it.
features.telemetry_use: Mark error/assertion procedures as cold to keep hot instrumentation code cache-efficient. Bounds checking, type assertions, and panics are marked @(cold) to minimize impact on normal execution. Improves telemetry overhead profile.

features.name: @(rodata)
features.what_it_does: Places a variable in read-only data section (.rodata). Enables compiler optimizations and memory protection (some platforms). Used for immutable configuration constants and lookup tables.
features.telemetry_use: Store immutable telemetry metadata (e.g., event names, type descriptions, configuration tables). Reduces runtime memory overhead and improves cache locality. Example: Argon2 parameters marked @(rodata) for crypto constants.
features.example:
@(rodata)
PARAMS_RFC9106 := Parameters{ memory_size = 2 * 1024 * 1024, passes = 1, parallelism = 4 }

features.name: @(require)
features.what_it_does: Marks a foreign (C/system) procedure as required. Compilation fails if the procedure cannot be resolved by the linker.
features.telemetry_use: Enforce availability of OS-level telemetry hooks (e.g., memory sanitizer APIs, debugger breakpoints, performance counter libraries). Example: Sanitizer hooks marked @(require) when Address Sanitizer is enabled.
features.example:
@(require)
__asan_unpoison_memory_region :: proc "system" (address: rawptr, size: uint) ---

features.name: @(disabled)
features.what_it_does: Disables a procedure or block at compile-time if CONDITION is true. Equivalent to #if !CONDITION wrapping. Used to optimize away code when features are disabled.
features.telemetry_use: Zero-overhead telemetry instrumentation: conditionally disable instrumentation at compile time. Example: @(disabled=ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT) skips assertion procs when asserts are disabled. Bounds checking and type assertions also use this pattern.
features.example:
@(disabled=ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT)
assert_contextless :: proc "contextless" (condition: bool, ...) { ... }

features.name: Source_Code_Location
features.what_it_does: Runtime structure capturing source location metadata: file path, line number, column, and procedure name. Passed to instrumentation hooks and error handlers. Obtained via #caller_location builtin.
features.telemetry_use: Metadata capture for every observed event: pinpoint where a call/error occurred in source. Enables source-level filtering, visualization, and correlation. Automatically populated by compiler in instrumentation_enter/exit calls and assertion failures.
features.example:
loc: Source_Code_Location = #caller_location  // Captured at call site
spall._buffer_begin(&ctx, &buf, "", "", loc)

features.name: Logger
features.what_it_does: Context-attached logging infrastructure. Provides a callback-based logging system with configurable levels and options (file, line, procedure, terminal color, etc.). Accessible via context.logger.
features.telemetry_use: Centralized structured logging for events. Enables swappable log backends (file, network, memory buffer). Levels (Info/Warning/Error/etc.) enable selective event capture. options bit_set controls metadata inclusion (file_path, line, procedure, colors).
features.example: context.logger.procedure(context.logger.data, .Info, "event", context.logger.options)

features.name: Logger_Proc
features.syntax: Logger_Proc :: #type proc(data: rawptr, level: Logger_Level, text: string, options: Logger_Options, location := #caller_location)
features.what_it_does: Procedure type for logger callbacks. Signature required for all custom logger implementations. Receives log level, formatted text, options, and source location.
features.telemetry_use: Implement custom telemetry backends: file logging, network streaming, in-memory ring buffers, etc. location parameter provides automatic source tracking without manual calls.
features.example: my_logger :: proc(data: rawptr, level: runtime.Logger_Level, text: string, options: runtime.Logger_Options, location := #caller_location) { fmt.println(location, text) }

features.name: Assertion_Failure_Proc
features.syntax: Assertion_Failure_Proc :: #type proc(prefix, message: string, loc: Source_Code_Location) -> !
features.what_it_does: Procedure type for assertion/panic callbacks. Signature for custom assertion handlers. Receives prefix (e.g., 'panic', 'assertion'), message, and source location. Must not return (arrow !).
features.telemetry_use: Hook assertion/panic events for crash reporting. Capture stack traces, memory state, or send diagnostics to remote service. All assertions, panics, and ensures route through this callback.
features.example: my_assertion_proc :: proc(prefix, message: string, loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location) -> ! { log_crash(loc, message); trap() }

features.name: @(builtin)
features.what_it_does: Marks a procedure as a built-in, available without explicit import. Compiler recognizes and may inline or optimize these specially.
features.telemetry_use: Not directly for telemetry, but used by telemetry-related procedures (container_of, copy, etc.). Enables zero-overhead abstractions used in profiler implementations.
features.example:
@builtin
copy_slice :: proc(dst, src: []$T) -> int { ... }

features.name: @(require_results)
features.what_it_does: Compiler warning if return value is not used. Ensures callers explicitly handle results. Helps catch ignored error codes or telemetry registration failures.
features.telemetry_use: Enforce that telemetry initialization/registration calls are not silently ignored. Example: allocator procs, temp_allocator_temp_begin (must save the Arena_Temp), logger/random_generator registration.
features.example:
@(require_results)
default_temp_allocator_temp_begin :: proc() -> Arena_Temp { ... }

features.name: ODIN_DEBUG
features.what_it_does: Boolean constant set to true when the -debug flag is passed to the compiler, enabling debug info generation and assertions
features.telemetry_use: Conditionally enable verbose instrumentation, deeper state captures, and assertion logging only in debug builds (zero overhead in release)

features.name: ODIN_OPTIMIZATION_MODE
features.what_it_does: Enum constant indicating optimization level (.None, .Minimal, .Size, .Speed, .Aggressive) set via -o flag; affects entire build
features.telemetry_use: Route timing/performance metrics differently based on opt level; enable sampling or low-overhead profiling in .Speed mode; detailed instrumentation in .None

features.name: ODIN_OS
features.what_it_does: Enum constant indicating target OS (.Windows, .Linux, .Darwin, .WASI, .Orca, etc.)
features.telemetry_use: Route telemetry events to OS-specific observability backends (ETW on Windows, SystemTap on Linux, os_log on Darwin); disable unsupported features

features.name: ODIN_ARCH
features.what_it_does: Enum constant indicating target CPU arch (.amd64, .arm64, .wasm32, .arm32, .i386, .riscv64)
features.telemetry_use: Enable arch-specific performance counters via CPU intrinsics (e.g. rdpmc on amd64, PMU on arm64); use arch-native cycle counter precision

features.name: ODIN_ENDIAN
features.what_it_does: Enum constant indicating endianness (.Little or .Big) of target platform
features.telemetry_use: Byte-order-aware serialization of captured telemetry values; avoid misinterpretation when analyzing cross-platform recordings
features.example: LITTLE_ENDIAN_PLATFORM :: true when ODIN_ENDIAN == .Little else false

features.name: ODIN_NO_BOUNDS_CHECK
features.what_it_does: Boolean constant set to true when -no-bounds-check flag suppresses runtime array/slice bounds checking
features.telemetry_use: Disable bounds-check instrumentation hooks in telemetry layer when -no-bounds-check is active; re-enable as warnings if needed for safety

features.name: ODIN_TEST
features.what_it_does: Boolean constant set to true when code is compiled via 'odin test' command (as opposed to normal 'odin build')
features.telemetry_use: Enable test-only telemetry instrumentation; embed test metadata (test name, expectations) in captured values; short-lived test runs don't pollute long-term telemetry

features.name: ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT
features.what_it_does: Boolean constant set to true when -disable-assert flag removes all assert() calls from program (compile-time, not runtime)
features.telemetry_use: When true, assertion telemetry layer is completely stripped; allows release builds to skip assertion recording entirely (zero-cost)

features.name: ODIN_NO_RTTI
features.what_it_does: Boolean constant set to true when -no-rtti flag inhibits generation of full runtime type information
features.telemetry_use: Disable automatic type introspection in telemetry (can't use type_info_of); fall back to manual type registration or pre-compiled type tables

features.name: ODIN_NO_TYPE_ASSERT
features.what_it_does: Boolean constant set to true when -no-type-assert flag disables type assertion checking program-wide
features.telemetry_use: Skip recording type assertion failures when feature is disabled; prevent spurious telemetry noise in robust/permissive builds
features.example: TYPE_ASSERTION_TELEMETRY_ENABLED :: true when !ODIN_NO_TYPE_ASSERT else false

features.name: ODIN_COMPILE_TIMESTAMP
features.what_it_does: i64 constant set to Unix nanoseconds at compile time; compatible with time.Time type
features.telemetry_use: Stamp every captured telemetry record with compile time; link captured values to exact binary build; correlate multi-build sessions
features.example:
build_time := time.Time{_nsec = ODIN_COMPILE_TIMESTAMP}
fmt.println("Binary built at:", build_time)

features.name: ODIN_VERSION
features.what_it_does: String constant containing Odin compiler version, typically 'dev-YYYY-MM'
features.telemetry_use: Tag all telemetry records with compiler version; track if telemetry format/interpretation changes across compiler versions
features.example: fmt.println("Telemetry from Odin", ODIN_VERSION)

features.name: ODIN_BUILD_PROJECT_NAME
features.what_it_does: String constant containing the name of the folder containing the entry point (e.g. 'demo' for examples/demo)
features.telemetry_use: Auto-stamp telemetry with project name; route observability data to project-specific sinks
features.example: project_telemetry_path := fmt.tprintf("telemetry/{}", ODIN_BUILD_PROJECT_NAME)

features.name: when statement (conditional compilation)
features.what_it_does: Compile-time if/else that includes or excludes code blocks based on constant compile-time expressions; evaluated at compile time, not runtime
features.telemetry_use: Completely remove telemetry code paths when disabled (zero assembly overhead); compile multiple telemetry strategies and pick one per build config
features.syntax: when CONDITION { /* code A */ } else when OTHER { /* code B */ } else { /* code C */ }

features.name: #config directive
features.what_it_does: Define a compile-time configurable constant with a default value; value can be overridden via -define flag
features.telemetry_use: Parameterize telemetry settings (buffer size, sample rate, enable/disable flags) at compile time without rewriting code
features.example:
TELEMETRY_BUFFER_SIZE :: #config(TELEMETRY_BUFFER_SIZE, 64 * Kilobyte)
TELEMETRY_ENABLED :: #config(TELEMETRY_ENABLED, ODIN_DEBUG)

features.name: #assert directive
features.what_it_does: Compile-time assertion; fails at compile time if expression is false, prevents code generation
features.telemetry_use: Validate telemetry schema/structure at compile time; ensure buffer layouts, type sizes are correct before any telemetry runs
features.example: #assert(size_of(Telemetry_Record) == 64, "Telemetry_Record must be 64 bytes for alignment")

features.name: #panic directive
features.what_it_does: Compile-time panic; emits a compiler error and stops compilation with a message
features.telemetry_use: Fail the build if incompatible telemetry config is detected (e.g. unsupported platform + required CPU feature)

features.name: #caller_location builtin
features.what_it_does: Injects Source_Code_Location (file, line, column, procedure) at call site automatically at compile time
features.telemetry_use: Automatically capture call site metadata (where telemetry was invoked) without manual parameter passing; enables stack trace reconstruction

features.name: Source_Code_Location struct
features.what_it_does: Runtime struct containing file_path, line, column (i32), and procedure (string); injected by #caller_location
features.telemetry_use: Attach precise source location metadata to every telemetry event; enables filtering/grouping by file, function, line; critical for live debugging
features.syntax: Source_Code_Location :: struct { file_path: string, line, column: i32, procedure: string }

features.name: read_cycle_counter intrinsic
features.what_it_does: Returns i64 CPU cycle counter (rdtsc on x86, cntvct_el0 on ARM); zero-overhead, single-cycle precision
features.telemetry_use: Ultra-low-overhead timestamping of captured values; enables microsecond/nanosecond-level performance telemetry without syscalls
features.example:
t0 := read_cycle_counter()
result := expensive_function()
t1 := read_cycle_counter()
cycles_elapsed := t1 - t0
record_latency_sample(cycles_elapsed)

features.name: read_cycle_counter_frequency intrinsic
features.what_it_does: Returns i64 CPU frequency in Hz; paired with read_cycle_counter to convert cycles → seconds
features.telemetry_use: Convert raw cycle counts to wall-clock time; scale latencies / throughputs to human-readable units
features.example:
freq_hz := read_cycle_counter_frequency()
freq_ghz := f64(freq_hz) / 1e9
cycles := read_cycle_counter()
time_seconds := f64(cycles) / freq_hz

features.name: volatile_load / volatile_store intrinsics
features.what_it_does: Memory load/store with volatile semantics; prevents compiler from optimizing away or reordering; forces read/write from/to actual memory
features.telemetry_use: Read/write telemetry shared buffers, lock-free queues, or memory-mapped observability endpoints without compiler interference

features.name: has_target_feature intrinsic
features.what_it_does: Runtime boolean check if CPU supports a named feature ("avx2", "sse4.1", etc.); also accepts procedure type with @(require_target_feature) / @(enable_target_feature)
features.telemetry_use: Conditionally enable/disable architecture-specific telemetry paths (e.g. AVX2-accelerated sampling); fall back to scalar when not available

features.name: type_of builtin proc
features.what_it_does: Returns runtime type information (^runtime.Type_Info) for any value; enables type introspection
features.telemetry_use: Inspect captured value's type at runtime; record type metadata alongside value; auto-format telemetry output

features.name: type_info_of builtin proc
features.what_it_does: Returns ^runtime.Type_Info for a given typeid; full reflection of type structure (fields, size, alignment, etc.)
features.telemetry_use: Introspect value types to auto-serialize telemetry (field names, sizes); validate captured data matches expected schema
features.syntax: ti := type_info_of(T) where T is a typeid

features.name: typeid_of builtin proc
features.what_it_does: Returns typeid for a given type (compile-time type → runtime typeid); pairs with type_info_of
features.telemetry_use: Correlate compile-time type names with runtime typeids; enable polymorphic telemetry dispatch via typeid
features.example:
T :: [10]i32
id := typeid_of(T)
ti := type_info_of(id)

features.name: Context struct with logger
features.what_it_does: Runtime context containing allocator, temp_allocator, assertion_failure_proc, logger, random_generator, user data
features.telemetry_use: Hook context.logger for global telemetry pipeline; install custom logger proc to intercept all log calls; store telemetry sink in context.user_ptr

features.name: Logger_Level enum
features.what_it_does: Severity levels for logging: Debug(0), Info(10), Warning(20), Error(30), Fatal(40); used to filter/categorize log events
features.telemetry_use: Tag telemetry events with severity; enable/disable recording based on min level; route fatal events to critical telemetry sink
features.syntax: Logger_Level :: enum uint { Debug=0, Info=10, Warning=20, Error=30, Fatal=40 }

features.name: Logger_Option enum & bit_set
features.what_it_does: Logger metadata flags: Level, Date, Time, Short_File_Path, Long_File_Path, Line, Procedure, Terminal_Color, Thread_Id
features.telemetry_use: Enable/disable automatic timestamp, file/proc metadata in logger output; control which contextual info is captured per log call
features.example:
context.logger.options = Logger_Options{
    .Long_File_Path,
    .Line,
    .Procedure,
    .Time,
    .Thread_Id,  // if available
}

features.name: ODIN_SANITIZER_FLAGS builtin
features.what_it_does: Bit_set of sanitizer flags set via -sanitize flag (Address, Memory, Thread); indicates which runtime checks are active
features.telemetry_use: Log which sanitizers are enabled; adjust telemetry overhead when Address/Thread sanitizers are active (they add significant overhead)

features.name: ODIN_NO_ENTRY_POINT
features.what_it_does: Boolean constant set to true when -no-entry-point makes main() optional; used for libraries or embedded code
features.telemetry_use: When true, telemetry init must be called explicitly (no auto-init at program start); affects initialization timing

features.name: read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: Reads the CPU's time stamp counter (TSC) — a high-resolution counter that increments every clock cycle. Returns a raw i64 value whose scale (nanoseconds or cycles) depends on interpretation via tsc_frequency or precise_time flag.
features.telemetry_use: Measure wall-clock time at instruction granularity for precise timing of hot sections; used internally by spall profiler for timestamp capture; basis for low-overhead frame/per-iteration measurements.

features.name: tick_now
features.what_it_does: Captures the current monotonic time as a Tick struct (wraps a nanosecond offset). Reads via platform-specific syscalls (clock_gettime on Linux/Unix; QueryPerformanceCounter on Windows) or TSC if available. Zero-overhead call; result is deterministic per-call but nondeterministic run-to-run.
features.telemetry_use: Record snapshots of monotonic time for frame timing, profiling intervals, or streaming trace timestamps. Replaces wall-clock time with monotonic guarantees. Low-overhead replacement for time.now() for perf-sensitive code.

features.name: tick_diff
features.what_it_does: Computes Duration (int64 nanoseconds) between two Tick snapshots. Pure arithmetic: end._nsec - start._nsec. Zero-overhead; deterministic given fixed Tick inputs.
features.telemetry_use: Calculate wall-clock duration of arbitrary code regions; feed into per-frame/per-call metrics. Basis for all timing-based observability (e.g., 'frame took 16ms').
features.example:
d := time.tick_diff(t_start, t_end)
if d > 33 * time.Millisecond { log.warnf("frame took %v", d) }

features.name: tick_since
features.what_it_does: Shorthand: calculates Duration from a Tick to *now*. Equivalent to tick_diff(start, tick_now()). Deterministic up to call time.
features.telemetry_use: Quick inline timing: measure elapsed time since an event without storing two snapshots; idiom for 'how long since X'.
features.example:
elapsed := time.tick_since(loop_start)
if elapsed > 1 * time.Second { break_and_report() }

features.name: tick_lap_time
features.what_it_does: Captures incremental duration since last lap (stored in *prev). Returns delta from prev to now, then updates prev = now. On first call (zero-initialized prev), returns 0. Used for iterative timing (e.g., 'time each frame' or 'time each chunk').
features.telemetry_use: Streaming per-iteration/per-frame timings without manual state. Feeds into telemetry buffer for frame time histograms or per-call overhead tracking; zero allocation.

features.name: SCOPED_TICK_DURATION
features.what_it_does: Deferred scope timing: captures current tick on entry, computes and stores Duration in *d on exit. Syntactic sugar for 'measure scope duration'.
features.telemetry_use: Automatic scope-level profiling with zero boilerplate. Collect per-scope timings in a map/array for telemetry. Compiler-inserted deferred call ensures precise exit timing.

features.name: tsc_frequency
features.what_it_does: Obtains CPU TSC frequency in Hz. First checks has_invariant_tsc(); if true, queries OS (_get_tsc_frequency). On fallback, sleeps for fallback_sleep, measures TSC delta, and computes Hz = tsc_delta * 1e9 / sleep_nanoseconds. Returns (hz, ok); ok=false if CPU lacks invariant TSC.
features.telemetry_use: Calibrate raw TSC reads (read_cycle_counter) to real time. Enables spall profiler to convert tick counts to nanoseconds. One-time or periodic calibration for traces that use raw cycle counters.
features.example:
hz, ok := time.tsc_frequency()
if ok { ns_per_cycle := 1_000_000_000 / hz }

features.name: has_invariant_tsc
features.what_it_does: Checks CPUID feature bit (x86-64) or returns true for ARM64. Invariant TSC means TSC runs at constant frequency independent of ACPI/frequency scaling, making it reliable for profiling.
features.telemetry_use: Predicate to decide whether raw TSC is trustworthy for timing. Skip TSC-based profiling if false; fall back to platform monotonic time.
features.example: if time.has_invariant_tsc() { use_tsc_for_profiling() } else { use_platform_timer() }

features.name: read_cycle_counter_frequency
features.what_it_does: Returns CPU frequency in Hz (on platforms that support it). Used to convert raw cycle counts into wall-clock time. Platform-dependent (available on x86/ARM; may return 0 on unsupported targets).
features.telemetry_use: Direct Hz lookup for cycle-to-nanosecond conversion, complementary to tsc_frequency. Preferred when available (no sleep calibration needed).
features.example:
freq := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter_frequency()
if freq > 0 { ns := (cycles * 1_000_000_000) / freq }

features.name: debug_trap
features.what_it_does: Emits a platform-specific breakpoint instruction (int3 on x86, brk on ARM). Causes debugger break if attached; otherwise raises SIGTRAP or similar. No-op under optimizations that elide it.
features.telemetry_use: Trigger telemetry event or flush on assertion/anomaly. Example: pause trace capture on invariant violation. Must be guarded by observability mode flags to avoid production overhead.
features.example: if observed_anomaly { intrinsics.debug_trap() }

features.name: expect
features.what_it_does: Compiler hint: tells LLVM the likely/expected value of a variable. Optimizes branch prediction and code layout. Returns val unchanged at runtime.
features.telemetry_use: Mark hot-path branches to minimize misprediction penalties; signals code expectations to help CPU prefetch and branch prediction. Indirect telemetry via reduced cache misses.
features.example: if intrinsics.expect(observed_type, Type_A) == Type_A { handle_common_case() }

features.name: likely / unlikely
features.syntax:
likely(val: $T) -> T where type_is_boolean(T)
unlikely(val: $T) -> T where type_is_boolean(T)
features.what_it_does: Compiler hints for branch probability. likely() hints the branch is taken; unlikely() hints it's not. Return val unchanged; purely for code generation.
features.telemetry_use: Optimize data collection paths: mark telemetry-enabled branches as likely/unlikely to reduce if-statement overhead. Example: 'if unlikely(telemetry_enabled) { collect(...) }'.
features.example: if intrinsics.likely(buffer_has_space) { append_event() } else { flush_and_retry() }

features.name: prefetch_read_data / prefetch_write_data
features.syntax:
prefetch_read_data(address: rawptr, #const locality: i32) // 0..=3
prefetch_write_data(address: rawptr, #const locality: i32)
features.what_it_does: Prefetch data at address into cache. locality (0-3) hints cache level: 0=L3, 3=L1. read_data hints load; write_data hints store+evict. Non-binding; CPU may ignore.
features.telemetry_use: Reduce cache misses in tight telemetry loops (e.g., trace buffer writes, histogram updates). Prefetch next histogram bucket or ring buffer chunk before use.
features.example:
next_bucket := &histogram[i+1]
intrinsics.prefetch_write_data(raw_data(next_bucket), 3) // L1 prefetch
record_value(histogram[i])

features.name: prefetch_read_instruction / prefetch_write_instruction
features.syntax:
prefetch_read_instruction(address: rawptr, #const locality: i32)
prefetch_write_instruction(address: rawptr, #const locality: i32)
features.what_it_does: Prefetch instruction cache (I-cache) at address. Hints CPU to load code bytes into instruction cache before execution.
features.telemetry_use: Prefetch callback procedures or hot telemetry functions in advance (rarely needed; compiler/CPU usually inlines/prefetches hot code).
features.example:
// Prefetch telemetry dispatch function before calling
intrinsics.prefetch_read_instruction(raw_data(telemetry_dispatch), 0)

features.name: atomic_load / atomic_load_explicit
features.syntax:
atomic_load(dst: ^$T) -> T
atomic_load_explicit(dst: ^$T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically load value from dst. Non-explicit is Seq_Cst; explicit accepts Relaxed/Acquire/Seq_Cst orders. Returns loaded value. No partial reads; safe for cross-thread reads.
features.telemetry_use: Read shared telemetry counters (enabled flags, buffer pointers, frame count) from concurrent threads without locks. Example: if telemetry_enabled (Relaxed read) { collect() }.
features.example:
enabled := intrinsics.atomic_load_explicit(&telemetry_enabled, .Relaxed)
if enabled { capture_event() }

features.name: atomic_store / atomic_store_explicit
features.syntax:
atomic_store(dst: ^$T, val: T)
atomic_store_explicit(dst: ^$T, val: T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order)
features.what_it_does: Atomically store val to dst. Non-explicit is Seq_Cst; explicit accepts Relaxed/Release/Seq_Cst orders. No partial writes.
features.telemetry_use: Update shared telemetry flags (pause/resume profiling, mode switches) atomically. Example: atomic_store(&profile_pause_flag, true) signals all threads to stop recording.
features.example: intrinsics.atomic_store_explicit(&buffer_head, new_head, .Release)

features.name: atomic_add / atomic_add_explicit
features.syntax:
atomic_add(dst: ^$T, val: T) -> T
atomic_add_explicit(dst: ^$T, val: T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically add val to *dst, return previous value. Fetch-then-modify semantics.
features.telemetry_use: Increment shared counters across threads: event count, byte processed, frame counter. Example: frames_rendered := atomic_add(&frame_counter, 1); if frames_rendered % 60 == 0 { report_fps() }.
features.example:
old_count := intrinsics.atomic_add_explicit(&event_count, 1, .Relaxed)
if old_count % 1000 == 0 { flush_batch() }

features.name: atomic_sub / atomic_sub_explicit
features.syntax:
atomic_sub(dst: ^$T, val: T) -> T
atomic_sub_explicit(dst: ^$T, val: T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically subtract val from *dst, return previous value.
features.telemetry_use: Decrement shared resource counters (e.g., 'active worker threads', 'inflight requests'). Used less than add but same semantics.
features.example: old_active := intrinsics.atomic_sub(&active_workers, 1)

features.name: atomic_exchange / atomic_exchange_explicit
features.syntax:
atomic_exchange(dst: ^$T, val: T) -> T
atomic_exchange_explicit(dst: ^$T, val: T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically swap *dst with val, return old value.
features.telemetry_use: Swap telemetry mode or buffer pointers: old_mode := atomic_exchange(&current_mode, new_mode). Enables lock-free mode transitions.
features.example: old_buffer := intrinsics.atomic_exchange(&active_buffer, &backup_buffer); flush_async(old_buffer)

features.name: atomic_thread_fence / atomic_signal_fence
features.what_it_does: Issue memory barrier without an associated operation. thread_fence orders across threads; signal_fence orders between thread and signal handler (no CPU instruction). Orders: Relaxed, Consume, Acquire, Release, Acq_Rel, Seq_Cst.
features.telemetry_use: Synchronize telemetry state visibility: after recording to a buffer, issue Release fence so other threads see it. Example: recording done, then atomic_thread_fence(.Release) ensures visibility.

features.name: spall.context_create
features.syntax:
context_create(filename: string, precise_time: bool, timestamp_scale: f64) -> (Context, bool)
context_create_with_sleep(filename: string, sleep := 2*Second) -> (Context, bool)
features.what_it_does: Initialize a spall trace file context. Writes magic+version+header to filename; calculates timestamp_scale (f64 nanoseconds per tick). precise_time=true uses read_cycle_counter; false uses platform monotonic time. _with_sleep variant auto-calibrates TSC frequency by sleeping.
features.telemetry_use: Begin trace capture session. Returns Context for use with buffer_create/SCOPED_EVENT. Enables streaming trace output to Spall profiler format (https://gravitymoth.com/spall/).
features.example:
ctx, ok := spall.context_create("trace.spall", true, (1.0 / tsc_hz) * 1e9)
defer spall.context_destroy(&ctx)

features.name: spall.buffer_create
features.syntax: buffer_create(data: []byte, tid: u32 = 0, pid: u32 = 0) -> (Buffer, bool)
features.what_it_does: Create a per-thread trace buffer. data must be >= 1024 bytes; tid/pid are thread/process IDs. Initializes buffer head to skip header; first_ts = 0. Buffer is thread-local and lock-free.
features.telemetry_use: Set up @(thread_local) trace buffer. One per thread; used with SCOPED_EVENT to record events. Flushed by buffer_destroy or on overflow.
features.example:
@(thread_local) spall_buffer: spall.Buffer
spall_buffer, ok = spall.buffer_create(make([]u8, spall.BUFFER_DEFAULT_SIZE), u32(sync.current_thread_id()))

features.name: spall.SCOPED_EVENT
features.syntax: SCOPED_EVENT(ctx: ^Context, buffer: ^Buffer, name: string, args: string = "", location := #caller_location) -> bool (deferred_in)
features.what_it_does: Deferred macro: records Begin event on entry (with current timestamp, name, args), End event on exit. Events streamed to buffer; buffer flushed to file on overflow. Captures call location if name="".
features.telemetry_use: Automatic scope-level trace capture. Feeds into Spall visualization showing call graph + timings. Zero manual event logging. Optionally pass #procedure for automatic naming.

features.name: spall.buffer_flush
features.what_it_does: Flush per-thread buffer to trace file. Writes buffer header + events to fd. Resets buffer.head and timestamps with 'Spall Trace Buffer Flush' annotation. Called automatically on SCOPED_EVENT overflow or manually.
features.telemetry_use: Periodic or on-demand trace flushing. Example: every frame or on pause signal. @(no_instrumentation) ensures trace overhead doesn't pollute profile itself.
features.example: spall.buffer_flush(&spall_ctx, &spall_buffer)

features.name: spall instrumentation_enter / instrumentation_exit hooks
features.syntax:
@(instrumentation_enter) hook_name :: proc(proc_addr, ret_addr: rawptr, loc: Source_Code_Location)
@(instrumentation_exit) hook_name :: proc(proc_addr, ret_addr: rawptr, loc: Source_Code_Location)
features.what_it_does: Compiler-inserted procedure calls at function entry/exit (if defined + @(instrumentation_enter/exit) attributes used). Receives procedure address, return address, and source location. Zero-cost if not defined.
features.telemetry_use: Automatic whole-program instrumentation: every function entry/exit auto-logged to trace. Example: spall_enter calls spall._buffer_begin; spall_exit calls spall._buffer_end. Creates comprehensive call graph trace without manual annotation.

features.name: runtime.Source_Code_Location
features.what_it_does: Metadata capturing source location: file path, line, column, and procedure name. Captured by #caller_location builtin. Passed to logger, assertion, and instrumentation hooks.
features.telemetry_use: Annotate all telemetry events with source context. Enables trace filtering by file/procedure. Example: spall events include location for source-level drill-down.
features.example: loc := #caller_location // {file_path: "main.odin", line: 42, column: 8, procedure: "foo"}

features.name: runtime.Logger
features.what_it_does: Logging sink with callback proc + metadata level + options (terminal color, file path, line, timestamp, thread ID). Stored in context.logger; used by all log.* calls.
features.telemetry_use: Plug custom telemetry sink: write logger_proc to capture log events + filter by level + include source location. Example: send log.info(...) events to trace buffer with location metadata.
features.example:
my_logger :: runtime.Logger{procedure = my_log_sink, lowest_level = .Debug, options = {.Time, .Procedure}}
context.logger = my_logger

features.name: log.* (debugf, infof, warnf, errorf, fatalf)
features.syntax:
debugf(fmt_str: string, args: ..any, location := #caller_location)
infof(...), warnf(...), errorf(...), fatalf(...)
features.what_it_does: Formatted logging at Level (Debug/Info/Warning/Error/Fatal). Routes to context.logger. Includes location + level filtering.
features.telemetry_use: Structured event logging: capture named events with tags/metadata. Example: log.infof("frame_start frame=%d fps=%.1f", frame_id, fps). Can be redirected to trace buffer via custom logger.
features.example: log.infof("event_count=%d buffer_used=%d%%", event_count, buffer_pct)

features.name: atomic_compare_exchange_strong / weak + explicit variants
features.syntax:
atomic_compare_exchange_strong(dst: ^$T, old, new: T) -> (T, bool)
atomic_compare_exchange_strong_explicit(dst: ^$T, old, new: T, success, failure: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> (T, bool)
atomic_compare_exchange_weak(...) // spurious failures OK
features.what_it_does: Atomic CAS: if *dst == old, swap to new and return (old, true); else return (*dst, false). strong = always correct; weak = may spuriously fail (arch-dependent). Explicit versions accept success/failure memory orders.
features.telemetry_use: Lock-free mode/buffer swaps: if cas(&active_mode, Old, New) { /* mode changed */ }. Enables lock-free state machines for profiling pause/resume.
features.example:
old_buf, ok := intrinsics.atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&current_buf, old_ptr, new_ptr)
if ok { flush_async(old_ptr) }

features.name: count_ones / count_zeros / count_trailing_zeros / count_leading_zeros
features.what_it_does: Bit-counting intrinsics; count set/unset bits or leading/trailing zeros. Hardware accelerated (POPCNT on x86, CLZ on ARM). Used for statistics.
features.telemetry_use: Analyze bit patterns in telemetry: count active samples in a bit-set of 64 threads, detect clustering, fast histogram summation via popcount.
features.example: active_threads := intrinsics.count_ones(thread_active_bitset) // O(1) vs O(n)

features.name: atomic_add
features.what_it_does: Atomically adds a value to memory and returns the old value. Lock-free on most platforms.
features.telemetry_use: Safely accumulate event counters from multiple threads (e.g., frame render count, event tally). Returns old value before increment for versioning.
features.example: counter := 0; old := sync.atomic_add(&counter, 1) // counter is now 1, old is 0

features.name: atomic_add_explicit
features.syntax: atomic_add_explicit :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically adds a value with explicit memory ordering control (Relaxed, Acquire, Release, etc.).
features.telemetry_use: Counter accumulation with tuned memory order: Relaxed for local counters (lower overhead), Release for cross-thread visibility.
features.example: sync.atomic_add_explicit(&counter, 1, .Relaxed) // fast non-synchronized add

features.name: atomic_load / atomic_load_explicit
features.syntax: atomic_load :: proc(dst: ^$T) -> T; atomic_load_explicit :: proc(dst: ^$T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically reads a value from memory. Seq_Cst by default; explicit version allows Relaxed for speed.
features.telemetry_use: Read current counter/metric value without tearing (partial reads). Relaxed reads for frequent sampling; Acquire reads to wait for cross-thread updates.
features.example: count := sync.atomic_load_explicit(&counter, .Relaxed) // fast snapshot

features.name: atomic_store / atomic_store_explicit
features.syntax: atomic_store :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T); atomic_store_explicit :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order)
features.what_it_does: Atomically writes a value to memory. Seq_Cst by default; explicit allows Release or Relaxed.
features.telemetry_use: Atomic flag setting (e.g., enable/disable telemetry globally). Release store ensures all prior writes visible to readers.
features.example: sync.atomic_store_explicit(&enabled, true, .Release)

features.name: atomic_compare_exchange_strong / atomic_compare_exchange_weak
features.syntax: atomic_compare_exchange_strong :: proc(dst: ^$T, old, new: T) -> (T, bool); atomic_compare_exchange_weak :: proc(dst: ^$T, old, new: T) -> (T, bool)
features.what_it_does: CAS: atomically compares location with old value; if equal, stores new value. Returns old value and success bool. Weak may spuriously fail.
features.telemetry_use: Lock-free state transitions (e.g., timestamp versioning, event batch handoff, flag flip). CAS loop for retries on weak failure.
features.example: ok := sync.atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&version, 0, 1).1 // if version was 0, set to 1

features.name: atomic_exchange
features.syntax: atomic_exchange :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T) -> T; atomic_exchange_explicit :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T, order: Atomic_Memory_Order) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically swap: stores new value, returns old value in one operation.
features.telemetry_use: Atomic buffer/batch swap (old snapshot <- new, return old for processing). Double-buffering without locks.
features.example: old_batch := sync.atomic_exchange(&current_batch, new_batch)

features.name: Atomic_Memory_Order enum
features.syntax: Atomic_Memory_Order :: enum { Relaxed, Consume, Acquire, Release, Acq_Rel, Seq_Cst }
features.what_it_does: Specifies memory ordering guarantees for atomic operations. Relaxed = no sync, Release/Acquire = cross-thread visibility, Seq_Cst = full ordering.
features.telemetry_use: Tune performance vs. correctness: Relaxed for unsynchronized per-thread tallies, Release for broadcasts, Seq_Cst only if total order needed.
features.example: sync.atomic_add_explicit(&counter, 1, .Relaxed) // faster, but unsync with other cores

features.name: atomic_thread_fence
features.what_it_does: Establishes memory ordering barrier without an associated atomic operation. Synchronizes memory across cores.
features.telemetry_use: Explicit sync point: ensure all prior telemetry writes visible before reader wakes. Used internally by condition variables.
features.example: sync.atomic_thread_fence(.Release) // flush telemetry writes to other threads

features.name: atomic_and / atomic_or / atomic_xor
features.syntax: atomic_and :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T) -> T; atomic_or :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T) -> T; atomic_xor :: proc(dst: ^$T, val: T) -> T
features.what_it_does: Atomically apply bitwise AND/OR/XOR, return old value.
features.telemetry_use: Lock-free flag sets/clears (bit mask for feature toggles, event types). Bitfield telemetry state.
features.example: sync.atomic_or(&flags, FLAG_HAS_NEW_FRAME) // atomically set frame-ready bit

features.name: Atomic_Mutex
features.what_it_does: Lock-based mutual exclusion. Hybrid: spins then uses futex for wait/wake on contention.
features.telemetry_use: Serialize writes to shared telemetry buffers (log ring buffers, event queues). Not zero-overhead but portable.
features.example: if sync.atomic_mutex_guard(&mutex) { buffer[idx] = event }

features.name: atomic_mutex_try_lock
features.what_it_does: Non-blocking attempt to acquire a mutex. Returns true on success, false if locked.
features.telemetry_use: Opportunistic sampling: try to snapshot metrics without blocking. Skip sample if contended.
features.example: if sync.atomic_mutex_try_lock(&stats_mutex) { frame_count = counter; sync.atomic_mutex_unlock(&stats_mutex) }

features.name: Atomic_RW_Mutex
features.syntax: Atomic_RW_Mutex :: struct { state: Atomic_RW_Mutex_State, mutex: Atomic_Mutex, sema: Atomic_Sema }
features.what_it_does: Reader-writer mutex: many readers OR one writer. Readers do lock-free CAS; writers use full lock.
features.telemetry_use: Telemetry read-heavy scenario: many threads read snapshot while single writer updates. High reader throughput.
features.example: if sync.atomic_rw_mutex_shared_guard(&rw_mutex) { snapshot = current_metrics }

features.name: Atomic_Sema (semaphore)
features.what_it_does: Semaphore: atomic count, wait/post. Wait blocks until count > 0, then decrements.
features.telemetry_use: Signaling: reader waits for telemetry writer to buffer events. Post-to-wake when batch ready.
features.example: sync.atomic_sema_wait(&data_ready) // telemetry reader waits; writer posts when batch complete

features.name: Atomic_Cond (condition variable)
features.what_it_does: Condition variable: thread waits/signals around a mutex. Wait releases mutex, reacquires on wake.
features.telemetry_use: Coordinated sampling: telemetry thread waits for event producer to signal 'batch ready'.
features.example: sync.atomic_cond_wait(&cond, &mutex) // drop lock, wait for signal

features.name: Wait_Group
features.syntax: Wait_Group :: struct { counter: int, mutex: Mutex, cond: Cond }
features.what_it_does: Synchronization: main waits for N worker threads to finish. Counter tracks pending work.
features.telemetry_use: Sync telemetry flush: main waits for all worker threads' telemetry batches to finish before export.
features.example: sync.wait_group_add(&wg, num_workers); ... sync.wait_group_wait(&wg) // all done, flush metrics

features.name: Barrier
features.syntax: Barrier :: struct { mutex: Mutex, cond: Cond, index: int, ... }
features.what_it_does: Multi-thread sync point: N threads wait until all N have reached the barrier.
features.telemetry_use: Stage-gated telemetry: measure per-stage (physics, render, audio). All threads barrier before advancing stage.
features.example: sync.barrier_wait(&barrier) // all worker threads sync here; then flush stage metrics

features.name: current_thread_id
features.what_it_does: Returns the unique ID of the calling thread.
features.telemetry_use: Tag telemetry events with thread ID. Separate per-thread buckets for lock-free accumulation.
features.example: tid := sync.current_thread_id(); metrics[tid].frame_count += 1

features.name: tick_now
features.what_it_does: Capture current high-resolution monotonic timestamp. Nanosecond precision.
features.telemetry_use: Record event timestamp. No wall-clock meaning, but stable for duration measurement (tick_diff). Never goes backwards.
features.example: t := time.tick_now() // capture frame start

features.name: tick_diff
features.what_it_does: Compute elapsed Duration between two Ticks. Handles wrap-around.
features.telemetry_use: Frame time, operation latency. Convert timestamps to wall durations.
features.example: elapsed := time.tick_diff(frame_start, time.tick_now())

features.name: tick_since
features.what_it_does: Shorthand for tick_diff(start, tick_now()). Returns elapsed time since start.
features.telemetry_use: Quick latency sample. How long since event X?
features.example: rendering_time := time.tick_since(render_start)

features.name: tick_lap_time
features.what_it_does: Atomically read diff from prev tick, store current tick, return elapsed. Zero if prev uninitialized.
features.telemetry_use: Rolling per-frame delta without explicit start. Lap timing loop: each call = frame elapsed since last call.
features.example: frame_delta := time.tick_lap_time(&prev_tick) // on loop, gets frame time each iteration

features.name: Tick (monotonic timestamp type)
features.what_it_does: High-resolution monotonic time value. Opaque; only tick_* procs interpret it.
features.telemetry_use: Store event timestamp. Does not correlate to wall time, but differences yield accurate durations across threads.
features.example: event_time: time.Tick; event_time = time.tick_now()

features.name: time.now (wall clock)
features.what_it_does: Return current wall-clock time (Unix epoch nanoseconds). Can go backwards (NTP adjustment).
features.telemetry_use: Correlate telemetry to wall time. Not recommended for timing (use tick_now). Deterministic only on replay.
features.example: wall_time := time.now() // record log entry timestamp

features.name: Duration (nanosecond precision)
features.what_it_does: Signed nanosecond duration. Literal constants: Nanosecond, Microsecond, Millisecond, Second, Minute, Hour.
features.telemetry_use: Store measured elapsed time. Zero-overhead; just i64.
features.example: frame_time: time.Duration; frame_time = time.tick_since(frame_start)

features.name: read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: Read CPU TSC (x86) or CNTVCT (ARM). Cycles, not nanoseconds. Very fast but non-portable.
features.telemetry_use: Extreme precision perf sampling. Divide by tsc_frequency to get nanoseconds. Not wall-time correlated.
features.example: cycles := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter(); ns = cycles / (tsc_freq / 1e9)

features.name: tsc_frequency
features.what_it_does: Obtain CPU TSC frequency in Hz. Returns ok=false if invariant TSC not available.
features.telemetry_use: Convert TSC deltas to ns. Calibrate on startup. Requires modern CPU (x86 with invariant TSC, ARM).
features.example: hz, ok := time.tsc_frequency(); if ok { ns = (tsc_end - tsc_start) / (hz / 1e9) }

features.name: has_invariant_tsc
features.what_it_does: Check if CPU has invariant TSC (constant freq independent of ACPI state).
features.telemetry_use: Gate TSC-based measurements. Fallback to tick_now if not available.
features.example: if time.has_invariant_tsc() { use_tsc_timing() } else { use_tick_timing() }

features.name: Stopwatch
features.syntax: Stopwatch :: struct { running: bool, _start_time: Tick, _accumulation: Duration }
features.what_it_does: Cumulative timer: start/stop/reset. Tracks total elapsed across multiple runs.
features.telemetry_use: Frame budget tracking. Sum of partial measurements (e.g., total render time across frame stages).
features.example: sw: time.Stopwatch; time.stopwatch_start(&sw); ...; time.stopwatch_stop(&sw); total := time.stopwatch_duration(sw)

features.name: @thread_local attribute
features.what_it_does: Declare a variable that is local to each thread. Each thread has its own copy; no synchronization needed.
features.telemetry_use: Per-thread event buffers, counters, temp storage. Zero-overhead; no locks. Requires cleanup on thread exit.
features.example: @(thread_local) local_buffer: [1024]Event

features.name: cpu_relax
features.what_it_does: Issue a relaxation hint to CPU (PAUSE on x86). Reduces power, yields to hyperthreading twin.
features.telemetry_use: Spin-wait optimization. Call in tight loops waiting for telemetry flag. Reduces CPU burn.
features.example: for !atomic_load(&flag) { sync.cpu_relax() } // spin waiting for signal

features.name: Context (runtime context)
features.syntax: Context :: struct { allocator, temp_allocator: Allocator, logger: Logger, random_generator: Random_Generator, user_ptr: rawptr, user_index: int, ... }
features.what_it_does: Thread-local context: allocators, logger, RNG. Every thread can set context.* for thread-local behavior.
features.telemetry_use: Stash thread-local telemetry sink in context.user_ptr. No global state, composable.
features.example: context.user_ptr = &my_thread_local_telemetry; ... log_event(e)

section: Data structures for series storage (telemetry observability)

features.name: Small_Array
features.what_it_does: Fixed-size stack-allocated array with dynamic length tracking. Behaves like a dynamic array but memory is pre-allocated on the stack up to N elements. Non-growing container.
features.telemetry_use: Capture rolling history of measurements without heap allocation. Ideal for fixed-window time-series (last N samples) in real-time telemetry where alloc frequency matters.
features.example:
history: Small_Array(1000, i64); small_array.push_back(&history, tsc_count)
Captures last 1000 cycle counts in O(1) bounded memory.

features.name: Queue
features.what_it_does: Dynamically-resizable double-ended queue backed by a [dynamic]T with ring-buffer semantics. O(1) push/pop both ends via offset tracking; auto-grows; can be initialized from fixed backing slice.
features.telemetry_use: Efficient time-series buffer (FIFO frame samples). Push new frame metrics at back; pop old metrics at front—no shifting. Ring-buffer layout is cache-friendly and avoids contiguous reallocs.
features.example:
q: queue.Queue(Metric); queue.init(&q, 60) // 60-frame rolling buffer
queue.push_back(&q, frame_metric)
old := queue.pop_front(&q) // oldest metric

features.name: intrusive_list (List, Node)
features.syntax:
List :: struct { head, tail: ^Node }
Node :: struct { prev, next: ^Node }
features.what_it_does: Doubly-linked list with O(1) insertion/removal. User embeds Node in a data structure; List maintains head/tail pointers. No separate allocation for link storage.
features.telemetry_use: Event log or sample chain where entries are added/evicted by policy (LRU, priority). Zero allocation overhead for link management; cache unfriendly (pointers scatter) but deterministic removal by policy.

features.name: Bit_Array
features.syntax: Bit_Array :: struct { bits: [dynamic]u64, bias: int, length: int, free_pointer: bool }
features.what_it_does: Dynamic bit-vector backed by [dynamic]u64 words. Efficiently packs boolean state at bit granularity. Auto-resizes on set(). Iterators for all/set/unset bits.
features.telemetry_use: Cheap track of per-sample boolean flags (e.g., sample.is_anomaly, sample.is_outlier) at ~1 bit/sample cost. Iteration over set bits identifies anomalous samples fast.

features.name: [dynamic]T (dynamic array)
features.what_it_does: Runtime-resizable array with len/cap. Backed by Raw_Dynamic_Array (data ptr, len, cap, allocator). Auto-grows on append; can delete() to free.
features.telemetry_use: Unbounded time-series buffer. Append samples over session lifetime; transmute to Raw_Dynamic_Array for introspection of allocation state; delete once session ends.

features.name: map[K]V (hash map)
features.syntax: map[K]V where K is valid_map_key and V is any type
features.what_it_does: Hash map with type-erased storage (Raw_Map has 64-byte-aligned data pointer encoding capacity in low bits). O(1) insert/lookup avg; auto-grows; can delete() to free.
features.telemetry_use: Aggregate samples by key (e.g., map[string]Histogram for per-subsystem metrics). Fast O(1) lookup to update histogram bins. transmute to Raw_Map to introspect load factor.
features.example:
histograms := make(map[string]Histogram)
if h, ok := histograms[subsystem_name]; ok { histogram.record(&h, sample_value) }

features.name: #soa (struct-of-arrays)
features.what_it_does: Compiler-synthesized memory layout: instead of array-of-structs (AoS), stores each field in separate contiguous array. soa_zip(field_slices) -> #soa[]Struct; soa_unzip(soa) -> (field_slices...). Cache-optimal for columnar access.
features.telemetry_use: High-performance time-series with columnar access: #soa[dynamic]Sample stores all timestamps together, all values together. Iterate-by-column avoids cache misses when scanning one field over many samples.
features.example:
Sample :: struct { ts: i64, value: f64, flags: u32 }
samples: #soa[dynamic]Sample
append(&samples, {ts, value, flags})
ts_slice, vals, _ := soa_unzip(samples[:]) // fast columnar access

features.name: Tick (monotonic time)
features.what_it_does: Opaque monotonic time snapshot (nanoseconds relative). Cheap to read (tick_now()); use tick_diff(start, end) to compute Duration without wall-clock jitter.
features.telemetry_use: Timestamp each sample with tick_now() at capture. tick_diff() to compute elapsed time between samples deterministically; immune to clock adjustments.

features.name: Duration
features.what_it_does: Opaque signed duration type (i64 ns). Supports arithmetic (tick_add, tick_diff). Constants: Second, Millisecond, Microsecond, Nanosecond.
features.telemetry_use: Store per-sample latency or elapsed time as Duration. Serialize or aggregate durations; compare without floating-point drift.
features.example:
lat: Duration = time.tick_diff(start_tick, end_tick)
if lat > 100 * time.Millisecond { /* slow sample */ }

features.name: SCOPED_TICK_DURATION
features.what_it_does: Deferred macro: captures tick at scope entry, writes duration at scope exit. Measures block execution time automatically.
features.telemetry_use: Measure latency of critical sections without manual timer start/stop calls. Zero-overhead when called; captures wall-clock time with @deferred_in_out semantics.

features.name: read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: CPU TSC (Time Stamp Counter) raw read. Very fast (~10 cycles); on invariant-TSC CPUs, correlates linearly with wall time if frequency is known.
features.telemetry_use: High-resolution sample timestamps. If tsc_frequency() succeeds, convert TSC to nanoseconds. Far faster than system timer and has no syscall overhead.
features.deterministic: yes (on single CPU; subject to TSC skew on multi-socket systems without invariant TSC)

features.name: has_invariant_tsc / tsc_frequency
features.what_it_does: Query if CPU TSC is stable (invariant); if so, measure TSC→Hz frequency via OS API or calibration sleep. Frequency enables converting raw TSC to wall-time.
features.telemetry_use: At startup, call tsc_frequency() to calibrate. If it succeeds, all read_cycle_counter() calls can be converted to ns via multiply-shift (fast). If it fails, fall back to tick_now().

features.name: Benchmark_Options (with benchmark proc)
features.syntax: Benchmark_Options :: struct { setup, bench, teardown: procs; rounds, bytes, count, processed: int; duration, rounds_per_second, megabytes_per_second: output fields }
features.what_it_does: Harness to benchmark a proc: setup() → bench() repeatedly → teardown(). Measures elapsed duration and computes throughput (rounds/sec, MB/sec).
features.telemetry_use: Microbenchmark hotpaths during development. benchmark() auto-times and reports duration and throughput without manual instrumentation.
features.deterministic: yes (one run deterministic; variability across runs due to OS/cache)

features.name: spall (Spall_Context, Buffer, SCOPED_EVENT)
features.syntax:
context_create(filename: string) -> (Context, ok: bool)
buffer_create(data: []byte) -> (Buffer, ok: bool)
SCOPED_EVENT(ctx, buffer, name, args) deferred macro
features.what_it_does: Trace capture: writes Begin/End events to a binary file in Spall format (viewable in Spall trace viewer). SCOPED_EVENT measures block span; context_create handles file I/O.
features.telemetry_use: Capture frame-by-frame (or sample-by-sample) timing into a trace file for offline analysis. SCOPED_EVENT + spall is zero-overhead when not profiling; can be left in shipping code with ifdef disable.
features.deterministic: yes (trace output order and timestamps deterministic)
features.example:
ctx, _ := spall.context_create("trace.spall")
buf, _ := spall.buffer_create(make([]u8, 1<<20))
{ spall.SCOPED_EVENT(&ctx, &buf, "frame_update"); /* ... */ }
spall.buffer_destroy(&ctx, &buf)

features.name: Type_Info (and type_info_of)
features.syntax:
type_info_of($T: typeid) -> ^runtime.Type_Info
Type_Info :: struct { size, align: int; id: typeid; variant: union of Type_Info_* }
features.what_it_does: Runtime type reflection: query field names, types, offsets for any struct or union. Inspect array/dynamic/slice/map element types. Enables generic/automated serialization.
features.telemetry_use: Automatically walk a Sample struct at runtime: extract field names, types, sizes. Build a schema description without manual marshalling code. Enables self-describing telemetry schemas.
features.example: info := type_info_of(Sample); switch v in info.variant { case runtime.Type_Info_Struct: for f in v.fields { fmt.printf("%s: %v\n", f.name, f.type) } }

features.name: Raw_Dynamic_Array (transmute introspection)
features.syntax: Raw_Dynamic_Array :: struct { data: rawptr, len, cap: int; allocator: Allocator }
features.what_it_does: Type-erased view of [dynamic]T. Transmute any dynamic array to Raw_Dynamic_Array to read data pointer, len, cap, allocator without type loss.
features.telemetry_use: Query current allocation state (cap, len) of a time-series buffer. Compute remaining headroom or estimate memory footprint. Introspect allocator for talloc/pool info.
features.example:
samples: [dynamic]Sample
raw := transmute(runtime.Raw_Dynamic_Array) samples
fmt.printf("len=%d cap=%d headroom=%d bytes\n", raw.len, raw.cap, (raw.cap - raw.len) * size_of(Sample))

features.name: Source_Code_Location (#caller_location)
features.syntax:
Source_Code_Location :: struct { file_path, procedure: string; line, column: i32 }
#caller_location directive captures caller location
features.what_it_does: Automatic compile-time capture of caller's file, line, procedure name. Used in assertions, logging, errors. Passed as default proc argument.
features.telemetry_use: Instrument telemetry calls with source location. Tag samples with the code location that generated them (e.g., 'main.odin:42 in frame_update'). Post-process traces to attribute metrics to source.
features.example:
observe(value, loc = #caller_location) // caller's location auto-captured
// telemetry record: { value, file: 'game.odin', line: 123, proc: 'update' }

features.name: volatile_load / volatile_store
features.what_it_does: Memory-order-preserving load/store. Compiler will not hoist, CSE, or elide these accesses. Prevents optimization of observable values.
features.telemetry_use: Write telemetry flags/values to a shared memory location that external tools might read (e.g., debugger, profiler, or separate process). Ensures write is not optimized away.
features.example:
telemetry_value: i64 = 0
intrinsics.volatile_store(&telemetry_value, current_metric) // external tool can read it

features.name: atomic_* procs (atomic operations)
features.syntax: atomic_load, atomic_store, atomic_add, atomic_exchange, atomic_compare_exchange_* etc. with optional _explicit variants for memory order control
features.what_it_does: Lock-free atomic operations with optional memory-order guarantees (Relaxed, Acquire, Release, Seq_Cst). Enable multi-threaded telemetry without locks.
features.telemetry_use: Safely update shared telemetry counters from multiple threads. Use Relaxed order for throughput counters; Seq_Cst for ordering-critical state (e.g., enabled flag).
features.deterministic: yes (within memory-order semantics; output depends on interleaving but operations are atomic)

features.name: mem_copy_non_overlapping / mem_zero
features.syntax:
mem_copy_non_overlapping(dst, src: rawptr, len: int)
mem_zero(ptr: rawptr, len: int)
