features.what_it_does: Intrinsic memory operations. mem_copy_non_overlapping is faster (no overlap check). mem_zero is often a memset call but may be optimized to mov +zero in loops.
features.telemetry_use: Bulk-copy or zero-init telemetry buffers. Fast batch-clear of sample arrays. Avoids function-call overhead of C memcpy when size known at compile time.
features.example:
samples: [10000]Sample
intrinsics.mem_zero(raw_data(samples[:]), len(samples) * size_of(Sample)) // clear buffer fast

features.name: count_trailing_zeros / count_leading_zeros
features.syntax: count_trailing_zeros(x: T) -> T where T is integer
features.what_it_does: Bit-level intrinsics (LLVM cttz/ctlz). Return 0-based index of lowest/highest set bit, or bitwidth if x==0.
features.telemetry_use: Fast scan for anomalies or set flags in a Bit_Array or bit-packed sample flags. Find first anomaly via ctz on a word of flags.
features.example:
flags: u64 = 0b1010
lowest_idx := intrinsics.count_trailing_zeros(flags) // returns 1 (bit 1 is first set bit)

features.name: Context (allocator, temp_allocator, user_ptr, user_index)
features.syntax: Context :: struct { allocator, temp_allocator: Allocator; logger, random_generator: ...; user_ptr: rawptr; user_index: int }
features.what_it_does: Thread-local context carrying allocators, logger, and user data. Accessible via global context variable. New allocator pushes context for that scope.
features.telemetry_use: Store telemetry state in context.user_ptr or user_index (e.g., per-thread metric buffer or session ID). Access in any proc without parameters. Simplifies passing state through deep call stacks.
features.example:
telemetry_ctx := cast(^Telemetry_State)context.user_ptr
if telemetry_ctx != nil { observe(telemetry_ctx, sample) }

features.name: Logger (in context)
features.syntax: Logger :: struct { procedure: Logger_Proc; data: rawptr; lowest_level: Logger_Level; options: Logger_Options }
features.what_it_does: Pluggable logging sink in context. Call context.logger(level, text, options, #caller_location) via default. Custom logger_proc can write to file, ring-buffer, network, etc.
features.telemetry_use: Integrate telemetry events into the logging pipeline. Custom logger_proc writes telemetry records to a trace file alongside log messages. Zero-cost when logging is disabled.
features.example:
// In init: context.logger = Logger{ procedure = my_telemetry_logger, data = &telemetry_state }
// Later, log events appear in telemetry output via the custom logger

features.name: encoding/json.marshal
features.syntax: marshal(v: any, opt: Marshal_Options = {}, allocator := context.allocator, loc := #caller_location) -> (data: []byte, err: Marshal_Error)
features.what_it_does: Serializes an arbitrary value (via `any` type) to JSON bytes using reflection. Supports nested structs, arrays, maps, enums, unions. Handles custom user marshalers via typeid dispatch. Three JSON specs: JSON, JSON5 (comments, unquoted keys), MJSON (key=value style).
features.telemetry_use: Core serialization engine for telemetry records. Capture struct values with metadata (timestamp, location, value name) and emit to JSON/NDJSON streams or files. Deterministic output per value per run.
features.example: data, err := json.marshal(telemetry_record) or_return; // Emits {"timestamp": 1234567890, "frame": 42, "value": 3.14}

features.name: encoding/json.marshal_to_writer
features.syntax: marshal_to_writer(w: io.Writer, v: any, opt: ^Marshal_Options) -> (err: Marshal_Error)
features.what_it_does: Streams JSON serialization directly to an io.Writer (file, buffer, network socket). Avoids intermediate allocation. Reflection-based marshaling of arbitrary `any` values.
features.telemetry_use: Zero-copy streaming of telemetry frames to disk/network. Write telemetry records directly to open file handles without buffering entire frames. Emit-per-tick workflows.
features.example: w := io.to_writer(file_stream); json.marshal_to_writer(w, frame_data, &opts); // Direct write, no heap allocation

features.name: encoding/json.User_Marshaler + register_user_marshaler
features.syntax:
User_Marshaler :: #type proc(w: io.Writer, v: any, opt: ^Marshal_Options) -> Marshal_Error
register_user_marshaler(id: typeid, marshaler: User_Marshaler) -> Register_User_Marshaler_Error
features.what_it_does: Pluggable type-specific marshalers. User can register custom serialization logic for any typeid (struct, enum, etc). Dispatch is done by typeid lookup at marshal time. Allows bespoke value encoding.
features.telemetry_use: Instrument custom types (game objects, physics states) with custom telemetry serialization. E.g. marshal a Vector3 as [x, y, z] instead of {x:_, y:_, z:_}. Zero overhead when not registered.
features.example: json.set_user_marshalers(new(map[typeid]json.User_Marshaler)); json.register_user_marshaler(type_info_of(Vector3).id, custom_vec3_marshaler);

features.name: encoding/csv.Writer
features.syntax:
Writer :: struct { comma: rune; use_crlf: bool; w: io.Writer; }
Writer.write(w: ^Writer, record: []string) -> io.Error
features.what_it_does: Streaming CSV writer. Escapes/quotes fields as needed. Writes one record ([]string) per call. Supports custom delimiters, CRLF control.
features.telemetry_use: Emit telemetry as tabular rows: timestamps, frame numbers, named values as CSV columns. Greppable, sortable, loadable into spreadsheets/DBs. Each row is a telemetry sample.
features.example: csv.writer_init(&w, file_writer); csv.write(&w, []string{"frame_42", "3.14", "1234567890"});

features.name: strconv.write_bits / write_bits_128
features.syntax: write_bits(buf: []byte, x: u64, base: int, is_signed: bool, bit_size: int, digits: string, flags: Int_Flags) -> string
features.what_it_does: Low-level integer-to-string conversion in any base (2–32). Writes to buffer; returns slice of formatted result. Supports prefix (0b, 0o, 0x), sign handling, arbitrary digit sets. Used internally by marshal.
features.telemetry_use: Convert raw numeric telemetry (frame count, memory bytes, cycle count) to strings for human-readable output or binary analysis. Basis for all int/uint serialization.
features.example: buf: [40]byte; s := strconv.write_bits(buf[:], 42, 16, false, 64, "0123456789abcdef", {.Prefix}); // "0x2a"

features.name: strconv.parse_i64 / parse_u64 / parse_int / parse_uint
features.syntax:
parse_i64(s: string, base := 0, n: ^int = nil) -> (value: i64, ok: bool)
parse_u64(s: string, base := 0, n: ^int = nil) -> (value: u64, ok: bool)
features.what_it_does: String-to-integer parsing with optional base inference (0x, 0b, 0o prefixes). Underscores allowed. Returns parsed value + bool (ok). Records consumed bytes via optional n.
features.telemetry_use: Deserialize telemetry records emitted as text (JSON/CSV). Parse frame IDs, timing values, counters from captured logs. Basis for telemetry log replay and validation.
features.example: n, ok := strconv.parse_i64("0x1234"); // n=4660, ok=true. Replay: parse each log line to reconstruct game state.

features.name: io.Writer / io.Stream
features.syntax:
Writer :: Stream :: struct { procedure: Stream_Proc; data: rawptr; }
Stream_Proc :: #type proc(stream_data: rawptr, mode: Stream_Mode, p: []byte, offset: i64, whence: Seek_From) -> (n: i64, err: Error)
features.what_it_does: Abstract stream interface for writing. Unified interface over files, buffers, sockets, multi-writers. Modes: Write, Flush, Close, Seek. Can be wrapped/composed.
features.telemetry_use: Write-once abstraction for telemetry backends: file, socket, ring buffer, multi-output. Inject telemetry into any io.Writer (including custom). Zero-copy forwarding to downstream.
features.example: var w io.Writer = file_stream_or_buffer_or_network; json.marshal_to_writer(w, frame_data, &opts);

features.name: time.Time
features.syntax:
Time :: struct { _nsec: i64; } // UNIX nanoseconds
now() -> Time
features.what_it_does: Absolute wall-clock time (UNIX epoch, nanosecond precision). Covers 1677–2262 date range. Platform-specific backend (_now). Convert to ISO8601/RFC3339 via time/datetime package.
features.telemetry_use: Timestamp each telemetry event with wall-clock time. Correlate telemetry across machines/sessions via absolute time. Emit as ISO8601 string in telemetry records.
features.example: t := time.now(); ts_str := time.to_rfc3339(t); // Emit as "2026-06-23T12:34:56.789Z"

features.name: time.Tick / tick_now / tick_diff
features.what_it_does: Monotonic high-resolution timer (not affected by clock adjustments). Relative, not absolute. Useful for measuring frame/sample deltas. tick_diff returns elapsed Duration (i64 nanos).
features.telemetry_use: Measure frame time, latency, spike detection, per-sample overhead. Monotonic so safe for cross-event timing. Emit tick_diff(prev, now) as frame duration in telemetry.
features.example: start := time.tick_now(); /* work */; elapsed := time.tick_diff(start, time.tick_now()); // Deterministic duration

features.name: time.SCOPED_TICK_DURATION
features.what_it_does: Deferred auto-timing directive. Captures duration of current scope in d. Deferred proc writes final tick_diff to d at scope exit.
features.telemetry_use: Zero-boilerplate automatic frame/phase timing. Emit d after scope: `{ SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&dur); /* frame code */; telemetry_emit(dur); }`
features.example: { SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&frame_time); /* frame work */; } // frame_time populated at exit

features.name: reflect.type_info_base / reflect.struct_field_* / reflect.enum_name_from_value_any
features.syntax:
type_info_base(id: typeid) -> ^Type_Info
struct_field_at(T: typeid, i: int) -> Struct_Field
struct_field_names(T: typeid) -> []string
enum_name_from_value_any(value: any) -> (name: string, ok: bool)
features.what_it_does: Runtime type introspection. Extract struct fields (names, types, offsets, tags), enum value→name mapping, type variant info. Tags support (e.g. json:"..."). Reflect over any typeid.
features.telemetry_use: Auto-instrument: iterate struct fields, emit name+value pairs. Reconstruct type metadata in telemetry (field names, enum names) without manual annotation. Generic telemetry capture.
features.example: info := reflect.type_info_base(type_info_of(some_struct).id); names := reflect.struct_field_names(some_struct.id); // Emit {field_names[i]: field_values[i]}

features.name: any type
features.what_it_does: Type-erased value container: (data: rawptr, id: typeid). Enables generic capture of any value + its type. Pairs with reflect/marshal to recover type info at runtime.
features.telemetry_use: Capture heterogeneous telemetry: pass any value to generic log/emit function. Encoder uses typeid to dispatch correct serialization logic. Build variable-schema telemetry.
features.example: v: any = some_value; info := type_info_of(v.id); // Recover type, then reflect or marshal

features.name: log.log / log.logf (context.logger)
features.syntax:
log(level: Level, args: ..any, sep := " ", location := #caller_location)
logf(level: Level, fmt_str: string, args: ..any, location := #caller_location)
Logger_Proc :: #type proc(data: rawptr, level: Level, text: string, options: Logger_Options, location := #caller_location)
features.what_it_does: Pluggable structured logging via context.logger. Levels: Debug/Info/Warning/Error/Fatal. Options bitmask (Date, Time, File, Line, Procedure, Color). Custom logger_proc can redirect/filter/transform. Call location auto-captured.
features.telemetry_use: Instrument gameplay with log.info/debug calls. Custom logger outputs to telemetry sink (JSON, CSV, network). Automatic location (source file + line). Structured per-level filtering/routing.
features.example: log.info("frame", frame_num, "value", value); // Logger emits structured record with Level, text, location

features.name: Source_Code_Location
features.syntax:
Source_Code_Location :: struct { file_path: string; line: int; column: int; procedure: string; }
#caller_location built-in
features.what_it_does: Captures source location (file, line, column, proc name) at call site. Built-in #caller_location directive injects at compile time. Used by assert, log, allocator tracking.
features.telemetry_use: Tag each telemetry event with source location (where measurement occurred). Pinpoint which frame method, physics sub-step, or render pass emitted the telemetry. Automatic callsite metadata.
features.example: loc := #caller_location; // Captures {file_path, line, column, procedure}. Emit in telemetry record.

features.name: fmt.Info / fmt.User_Formatter + register_user_formatter
features.syntax:
User_Formatter :: #type proc(fi: ^Info, arg: any, verb: rune) -> bool
register_user_formatter(id: typeid, formatter: User_Formatter) -> Register_User_Formatter_Error
features.what_it_does: Custom printf-style formatters per typeid. Verb-dispatch (d, v, x, etc). Formatter inspects Info state (width, precision, flags). Used by fmt.printf, fmt.sprintf.
features.telemetry_use: Format telemetry values with custom precision/width (e.g. %.2f for floats, %x for hex IDs). Lightweight text emission for logs. Alternative to JSON when streaming text.
features.example: fmt.set_user_formatters(new(map[typeid]fmt.User_Formatter)); register custom Vector3 formatter → fmt.printf("pos=%v", pos) emits custom format

features.name: intrinsics.read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: CPU cycle counter (TSC on x86, equivalent on ARM). High-precision timing (nanosecond-scale on modern CPUs). Not affected by OS scheduling. Wraps around on 64-bit boundary.
features.telemetry_use: Measure micro-timing: instruction-level latency, cache effects, stalls. Emit raw cycle counts in telemetry. Correlate with tick_now() for calibration. CPU-precise profiling.
features.example: start := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter(); /* code */; cost := intrinsics.read_cycle_counter() - start; // Raw cycle cost

features.name: intrinsics.debug_trap
features.what_it_does: Issue CPU debug trap (INT3 on x86). If debugger attached, halts execution. No-op if not debugging.
features.telemetry_use: Conditional telemetry assertions: `if anomaly { debug_trap(); }` to break into debugger when telemetry detects out-of-spec values. Conditional instrumentation.
features.example: if frame_time > max_frame_budget { debug_trap(); telemetry_emit(OVERBUDGET, frame_time); }

features.name: time.Stopwatch / stopwatch_start / stopwatch_stop
features.what_it_does: Stateful interval timer. Accumulates total Duration across multiple start/stop pairs. Useful for measuring total time across non-contiguous phases.
features.telemetry_use: Track cumulative time spent in a system across frame lifecycle (input → physics → render). Call start/stop at phase boundaries; emit sw._accumulation at frame end.
features.example: stopwatch_start(&physics_timer); /* physics */; stopwatch_stop(&physics_timer); /* logic */; stopwatch_start(&physics_timer); /* more physics */; stopwatch_stop(&physics_timer); // Emit total physics time

features.name: encoding/json.Marshal_Options
features.syntax: Marshal_Options :: struct { spec: Specification; pretty: bool; use_spaces: bool; spaces: int; write_uint_as_hex: bool; sort_maps_by_key: bool; use_enum_names: bool; ... }
features.what_it_does: Configurable JSON output: compact vs. pretty-printed, enum-as-name vs. enum-as-value, hex uint, map sorting, MJSON/JSON5 variants. Per-marshal customization.
features.telemetry_use: Control telemetry record verbosity: compact for streaming, pretty for logs. Output enum names (readable) vs. values (compact). Sort maps for deterministic output across runs.
features.example: opts := json.Marshal_Options{pretty: true, use_enum_names: true}; json.marshal(data, opts); // Readable enum names, formatted

features.name: time.benchmark + Benchmark_Options
features.syntax:
Benchmark_Options :: struct { setup, bench, teardown: proc(...); rounds, bytes, count, processed: int; duration: Duration; ... }
benchmark(options: ^Benchmark_Options, allocator := context.allocator) -> Benchmark_Error
features.what_it_does: Standard benchmarking harness. Runs setup → bench (timed) → teardown. Computes duration, rounds/sec, MB/sec. User-supplied setup/teardown for initialization.
features.telemetry_use: Structured performance benchmarking. Emit benchmark results as telemetry: name, duration, throughput. Automated regression detection by comparing successive benchmark runs.
features.example: bench_opts := time.Benchmark_Options{bench: my_benchmark_fn}; time.benchmark(&bench_opts); telemetry_emit(BENCHMARK, "name", bench_opts.duration, bench_opts.rounds_per_second);

features.name: terminal.is_terminal
features.what_it_does: Detects whether a File (stdout/stderr/stdin) is attached to a terminal/TTY. Returns false if redirected to file/pipe.
features.telemetry_use: Determines if output is interactive (terminal) vs non-interactive (redirected to file/pipe). Used to decide whether to emit ANSI codes, colored output, or progress indicators. Critical gate for telemetry UI.
features.example: if terminal.is_terminal(os.stdout) { fmt.println(ansi.CSI + ansi.FG_GREEN + ansi.SGR + "Online") }

features.name: terminal.color_depth
features.what_it_does: Module-level constant set at program init. Reports the terminal's color capability: None (0), Three_Bit (8 colors), Four_Bit (16), Eight_Bit (256), or True_Color (24-bit RGB). Auto-detected from Windows VTP mode, environment vars (COLORTERM, TERM), or fallback.
features.telemetry_use: Gate ANSI color output: skip if .None, use bright colors if .Four_Bit+, emit RGB codes only if .True_Color. Respects NO_COLOR env var (disables all color).
features.example: when terminal.color_depth >= .Eight_Bit { fmt.println(ansi.CSI + ansi.FG_COLOR_8_BIT + ";196" + ansi.SGR + "Red") }

features.name: terminal.color_enabled
features.what_it_does: Module-level bool set at init. True if color output is enabled (color_depth > None AND NO_COLOR env var is absent).
features.telemetry_use: Simple guard: `if terminal.color_enabled { ... emit color ANSI ... }`. Respects both capability detection and user override (NO_COLOR).
features.example: fmt.println(terminal.color_enabled ? ansi.CSI + ansi.FG_CYAN + ansi.SGR + "Enabled" : "Disabled")

features.name: terminal.Color_Depth
features.syntax: Color_Depth :: enum { None, Three_Bit, Four_Bit, Eight_Bit, True_Color }
features.what_it_does: Enum of supported color depths. Ordered; comparisons (>=, <=) check capability levels.
features.telemetry_use: Type for conditional color emission. Allows graceful fallback: 256-color codes on Eight_Bit+, bright ANSI on Four_Bit, no color on None.
features.example: match terminal.color_depth { .True_Color => emit_24bit_rgb, .Eight_Bit => emit_256_palette, .Four_Bit => emit_bright_ansi, .None => no_ansi }

features.name: os.is_tty
features.what_it_does: Lower-level TTY check. On Windows: checks if file type is FILE_TYPE_CHAR. On POSIX: calls isatty(fd). No environment variable checks.
features.telemetry_use: Raw platform check (terminal.is_terminal is the high-level wrapper). Use if you need to bypass color_depth logic and just detect raw TTY presence.
features.example: os.is_tty(os.stdout) // true if stdout is a terminal

features.name: os.lookup_env / os.get_env
features.syntax: lookup_env :: proc { lookup_env_alloc(key: string, allocator: Allocator) -> (value: string, found: bool), lookup_env_buf(buf: []u8, key: string) -> (value: string, err: Error) }
features.what_it_does: Read environment variable. lookup_env returns (value, bool) distinction; lookup_env_buf uses user-provided buffer (non-allocating, max 512 utf-16 on Windows). get_env wraps lookup_env, returns empty string if not found.
features.telemetry_use: Check config env vars: COLORTERM (truecolor/24bit), TERM (term-256color, term-16color, etc), NO_COLOR. Also TERM_PROGRAM (iTerm, etc for platform-specific features), DEBUG_LEVEL, LOG_FILE.
features.example: buf: [128]u8; if no_color, err := os.lookup_env(buf[:], "NO_COLOR"); err == nil { skip_colors = no_color != "" }

features.name: sys/windows.GetConsoleMode / SetConsoleMode
features.syntax: GetConsoleMode :: proc(hConsoleHandle: HANDLE, lpMode: LPDWORD) -> BOOL; SetConsoleMode :: proc(hConsoleHandle: HANDLE, dwMode: DWORD) -> BOOL
features.what_it_does: Windows console API. GetConsoleMode reads current console mode flags. SetConsoleMode sets flags (returns bool success). Used to enable ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING (0x0004) for ANSI support.
features.telemetry_use: Enable Windows ANSI: call GetConsoleMode, OR with ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING | ENABLE_PROCESSED_OUTPUT, call SetConsoleMode. Terminal module does this on init (is auto).
features.example: handle := windows.GetStdHandle(windows.STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE); if windows.GetConsoleMode(handle, &mode) { windows.SetConsoleMode(handle, mode | windows.ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING) }

features.name: sys/windows.GetStdHandle
features.what_it_does: Gets Windows console handle for stdout/stderr/stdin. which = STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE / STD_ERROR_HANDLE / STD_INPUT_HANDLE. Returns INVALID_HANDLE on error.
features.telemetry_use: Obtain HANDLE for stdout/stderr to enable ANSI mode via SetConsoleMode. Called on Windows init to prep terminal.
features.example: handle := windows.GetStdHandle(windows.STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE)

features.name: ansi.* (ANSI constants)
features.syntax: CSI :: "\e[" | SGR :: "m" | ESC :: "\e" | FG_COLOR_24_BIT :: "38;2" | etc. (80+ constants)
features.what_it_does: Pre-built ANSI escape sequence components. CSI (Control Seq Introducer) + SGR (Select Graphic Rendition) form color/style codes. Includes 16 basic colors (FG_BLACK..FG_WHITE), bright variants, 256-palette (FG_COLOR_8_BIT), 24-bit RGB (FG_COLOR_24_BIT), text styles (BOLD, UNDERLINE, etc), cursor control (CUU, CUF, CHA, etc).
features.telemetry_use: Build telemetry output strings: `ansi.CSI + ansi.FG_CYAN + ansi.SGR + "msg" + ansi.CSI + ansi.RESET + ansi.SGR` for colored text. Cursor movement for progress bars/live updates (CUP, CUF, ED). Hide/show cursor (DECTCEM_HIDE / DECTCEM_SHOW).
features.example: fmt.println(ansi.CSI + ansi.BOLD + ";" + ansi.FG_GREEN + ansi.SGR + "Status: OK" + ansi.CSI + ansi.RESET + ansi.SGR); fmt.println(ansi.CSI + ansi.FG_COLOR_24_BIT + ";255;0;0" + ansi.SGR + "Red text"); fmt.print(ansi.CSI + "2J"); // clear screen

features.name: time.now
features.what_it_does: Returns current wall-clock Time (nanosecond precision, Unix epoch). Monotonically increasing on same system.
features.telemetry_use: Timestamp telemetry samples: `t := time.now(); record_metric(t, value)`. Wall-clock for absolute time logging (when did event occur), ISO 8601 formatting.
features.example: t := time.now(); fmt.println(time.time_to_unix_nano(t))

features.name: time.tick_now / time.tick_diff
features.syntax: tick_now :: proc "contextless" () -> Tick; tick_diff :: proc "contextless" (start, end: Tick) -> Duration
features.what_it_does: High-resolution monotonic clock. Tick is opaque; tick_now() captures current time, tick_diff(start, end) computes elapsed Duration (nanosecond precision). Never goes backward, immune to system clock adjustments.
features.telemetry_use: Precise frame/operation timing for observability: `t := tick_now(); do_work(); elapsed := tick_diff(t, tick_now()); record_frame_time(elapsed)`. Better than time.now for relative measurements.
features.example: start := time.tick_now(); compute(); elapsed := time.tick_diff(start, time.tick_now()); fmt.println(time.duration_milliseconds(elapsed), "ms")

features.name: time.Tick
features.what_it_does: Monotonic time point. Opaque; values only meaningful when diffed. Backed by OS monotonic clock (clock_gettime CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Unix, QueryPerformanceCounter on Windows).
features.telemetry_use: Container for frame/operation start times. Pass to tick_diff, tick_since, or SCOPED_TICK_DURATION for auto-measurement.
features.example: prev: time.Tick; elapsed := time.tick_lap_time(&prev); // incremental frame delta

features.name: time.Stopwatch
features.syntax: Stopwatch :: struct { running: bool, _start_time: Tick, _accumulation: Duration }
features.what_it_does: Coarse manual timer. Start/stop/reset lifecycle; accumulates total duration across multiple intervals. Not high-precision.
features.telemetry_use: Long-running measurements (session duration, frame budget tracking, profiler warmup). Record total time: `stopwatch_duration(sw)` (includes current run if still running).
features.example: sw: time.Stopwatch; time.stopwatch_start(&sw); do_work(); time.stopwatch_stop(&sw); fmt.println(time.duration_milliseconds(time.stopwatch_duration(sw)))

features.name: time.Duration
features.syntax: Duration :: distinct i64 (nanosecond precision); Nanosecond, Microsecond, Millisecond, Second, Minute, Hour
features.what_it_does: Signed i64 nanoseconds. Pre-defined constants (Second = 1e9 ns, Millisecond = 1e6 ns, etc). Can be negative.
features.telemetry_use: Represent elapsed time deltas in telemetry. Convert to human-readable: duration_seconds, duration_milliseconds, duration_nanoseconds. Format with time_to_string_hms.
features.example: d := time.tick_diff(t1, t2); ms := time.duration_milliseconds(d); fmt.println(ms, "ms")

features.name: time.read_cycle_counter
features.what_it_does: Raw CPU cycle counter (rdtsc on x86, similar on ARM). Wraps intrinsics.read_cycle_counter(). Varies with CPU frequency (not invariant unless CPU has invariant TSC). Monotonically increasing within a session.
features.telemetry_use: Ultra-high-resolution timing for hot-path profiling. NOT suitable for elapsed time (no scale to ns/us); only for cycle-count diffs (cache behavior, instruction count proxy). Combine with tsc_frequency() to convert to wall time if CPU has invariant TSC.
features.example: c1 := time.read_cycle_counter(); tight_loop(); c2 := time.read_cycle_counter(); cycles := c2 - c1

features.name: time.has_invariant_tsc / time.tsc_frequency
features.syntax: has_invariant_tsc :: proc "contextless" () -> bool; tsc_frequency :: proc "contextless" (fallback_sleep := 2*Second) -> (u64, bool)
features.what_it_does: Check if CPU has invariant TSC (constant frequency across power states). tsc_frequency returns freq in Hz if available, uses cpuid or fallback calibration (sleep & measure). Both return false/0 if unavailable.
features.telemetry_use: Precondition for converting cycle_counter diffs to wall time. If invariant: `cycles_to_ns = cycles * 1e9 / tsc_frequency`. Enables deterministic cycle-level telemetry on modern CPUs.
features.example: if has, ok := time.tsc_frequency(); ok { hz := has; ns_per_cycle := 1e9 / f64(hz) }

features.name: time.SCOPED_TICK_DURATION
features.what_it_does: Deferred macro: captures tick on entry, computes tick_diff on exit, writes Duration to d^. Zero-overhead measurement of scope execution time.
features.telemetry_use: Instrumentation: `{ d: time.Duration; defer time.SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&d) { ... work ...; fmt.println(d) } }`. Captures frame/function duration with zero manual calls if enabled.
features.example: { d: time.Duration; defer time.SCOPED_TICK_DURATION(&d) { do_expensive_work() }; fmt.println("Took:", time.duration_milliseconds(d), "ms") }

features.name: time.tick_since
features.what_it_does: Shorthand: tick_diff(start, tick_now()). Compute elapsed time since a Tick.
features.telemetry_use: Frame delta: `prev: Tick; ... loop: prev = tick_now(); frame_time := tick_since(prev) after first iter`. Simple elapsed-time queries.
features.example: t := time.tick_now(); time.sleep(10*time.Millisecond); elapsed := time.tick_since(t)

features.name: time.tick_lap_time
features.what_it_does: Incremental: compute tick_diff(prev^, now()), store tick_now() back in prev^. Returns 0 on first call (prev was zero-init). Stateful per-ptr.
features.telemetry_use: Per-frame delta recording loop: `prev: Tick; while running { elapsed := tick_lap_time(&prev); record(elapsed) }`. Automatic frame-to-frame accounting.
features.example: prev: time.Tick; for { frame_delta := time.tick_lap_time(&prev); record_frame_time(frame_delta) }

features.name: time.benchmark + Benchmark_Options
features.syntax: benchmark :: proc(options: ^Benchmark_Options, allocator := context.allocator) -> Benchmark_Error; Benchmark_Options :: struct { setup, bench, teardown: procs, rounds, bytes, count, processed: int, duration: Duration, rounds_per_second, megabytes_per_second: f64, ... }
features.what_it_does: Built-in benchmark harness. Calls setup, runs bench (measures elapsed), calls teardown. Computes duration, ops/sec, MB/s. Stores results in options.
features.telemetry_use: Codify performance telemetry: wrap perf-critical code in Benchmark_Options, run benchmark(), extract duration/throughput. Usable for automated perf regression detection.
features.example: opts := {bench = proc(opts, alloc) { for _ in 0..<opts.rounds { do_work() } }, rounds = 1000}; time.benchmark(&opts); fmt.println(opts.rounds_per_second, "ops/s")
